jobs.description:
About Us

Boundless Life is a family-focused living, working and academy operator building a new model for how families live, their children learn, and parents work around the world. Across eight global destinations — Sintra (Portugal), Syros (Greece), Tuscany (Italy), Andalusia (Spain), Kotor (Montenegro), Bali (Indonesia), Kamakura (Japan), and La Barra (Uruguay) — we offer families the infrastructure to spend one, three, or 6+ months living in a new country: fully furnished homes, dedicated coworking hubs, and our own academy project based learning programs for children ages 1.5 -14.9 years old.

Our members are professionals, entrepreneurs, remote workers, and their families who want their children to grow up as global citizens without pausing their careers or their kids' education. We are asset-light where we can be, hybrid where it makes sense, and long-term partners with our landlords and local communities in every market we enter.

The future of family life and work is global, seamless, and community-driven — and we are building it. Join us as we scale toward our next wave of destinations across Europe, Asia, and the Americas.

About The Opportunity

Boundless Life is seeking a highly capable Real Estate Legal Transaction Manager to join our Real Estate & Expansion team and support the growth of our global portfolio across eight active markets today, an active expansion pipeline.

The ideal candidate will bring solid, hands-on experience in commercial real estate legal practice — with a particular focus on complex, multi-jurisdictional lease negotiations and hybrid deal structures (leases with management, operating, or revenue-share components).

This role will serve as a dedicated legal transaction partner to the Real Estate & Expansion team, reporting directly to the General Legal Counsel and working shoulder-to-shoulder with our Global Head of Real Estate, in-house counsel, external local counsel, and business stakeholders across each market. A core focus of the role is the negotiation, drafting, and interpretation of commercial and residential leases, together with all associated ancillary documents — LOIs, addenda, side letters, management agreements, SNDAs, estoppels, guarantees, and building/regulatory authorizations.

Beyond transactional execution, the successful candidate will help build the legal-operational backbone of a fast-growing global platform: standardizing playbooks, coordinating local counsel across jurisdictions, and translating legal risk into commercially usable guidance for the business.

Boundless Life operates across eight very different legal environments — from Portuguese and Spanish commercial lease frameworks to Indonesian Hak Pakai regimes, Italian, Greek, and Montenegrin civil law traditions, and Japanese and Uruguayan market practice — with active expansion pipeline (France, Costa Rica) adding further complexity. Candidates must be comfortable quickly grasping the intricacies of new jurisdictions, working through unfamiliar frameworks with local counsel, and holding the commercial line while doing so.

This position reports to the General Counsel, with a strong working line into the Head of Real Estate & Expansion. Location is flexible (remote-friendly, EMEA time zone preferred), with regular travel expected to active and prospective markets.

Key Responsibilities

  • Transactional Execution: Lead the drafting and negotiation of a diverse deal flow, including commercial leases (education centers, coworking hubs, family lounges), residential portfolio leases and management agreements, LOIs, MOUs, lease amendments, SNDAs, estoppels, guarantees, and hybrid lease-plus-management structures. Ensure every document protects Boundless Life's commercial and operational interests while unblocking the growth pipeline.
  • Multi-Jurisdictional Coordination: Manage and quality-control external local counsel across our active markets (currently Portugal, Greece, Italy, Spain, Montenegro, Indonesia, Japan, and Uruguay), our active expansion markets (France, Costa Rica), and any new jurisdiction we enter. Own the relationship, the scope, and the output — including translating local legal advice into clear, actionable direction for the business.
  • Asset Management & Operational Support: Provide legal interpretation of the existing lease portfolio and day-to-day support to Operations, Finance, Local Hosts, and Community teams on lease questions, escalations, disputes, permits, and landlord communications.
  • Real Estate Due Diligence: Lead legal due diligence on new locations and strategic initiatives — identifying and pricing regulatory, title, zoning, ERP/permitting, tax withholding, and structural risks — and translating findings into go/no-go recommendations.
  • Playbook & Process Optimization: Help build the RE Legal function from the inside out: templates, redline playbooks by jurisdiction, approval workflows, contract repository standards, and lease management processes. Turn one-off work into repeatable systems.
  • Strategic and Practical Legal Advice: Deliver timely, commercially oriented legal advice to internal stakeholders across all levels — from Development Managers and Project Managers up to the CEO and Board — translating complex legal concepts into clear, risk-based recommendations the business can act on.
  • Dispute Management: Support the resolution of landlord, tenant, and vendor disputes across markets, working with local counsel where litigation, arbitration, or termination scenarios arise.

About You

  • Education: Law degree (JD, LLB, Licenciatura en Derecho, or foreign equivalent) from an accredited institution. LLM or dual-jurisdiction qualification is a plus.
  • Bar Admission: Qualified to practice law in at least one relevant jurisdiction.
  • Experience: Minimum of 5 years of direct experience in commercial real estate, contract management and leasing practice OR 7 years dealing with high volume complex commercial agreements. A background combining top-tier law firm training with in-house exposure is strongly preferred. Prior experience in hospitality, coliving, education, or multi-jurisdictional real estate portfolios is a significant plus.
  • Languages — Required: Excellent professional proficiency in both English and Spanish, spoken and written. Comfortable negotiating and drafting complex legal documents in both languages.
  • Languages — Strong Plus: Working proficiency in one or more of: Portuguese, Italian, French, or Japanese. Given the geographic footprint, any additional Boundless Life market language materially improves the fit.
  • Multi-Market Fluency: Demonstrated ability to quickly grasp the intricacies of new legal systems, distinguish market convention from negotiable position, and work effectively with local counsel across civil and common law jurisdictions.
  • Technical Mastery: Proven ability to identify novel and complex legal issues, escalate them appropriately, and translate them into clear, risk-based recommendations for both business and legal stakeholders.
  • Judgement & Ownership: Takes full ownership of work product. Operates effectively and independently with minimal oversight, while maintaining a high standard of accuracy, quality, and efficiency.
  • Organizational Skills: Exceptional organization and prioritization. Comfortable holding many parallel workstreams — often across multiple time zones and markets — without dropping detail or missing deadlines.
  • Travel: Willing and able to travel regularly (indicatively 15–25% of the time) to active and prospective markets for site visits, negotiations, and closings.
  • Cultural Fit: Collaborative, low-ego, mission-aligned. Comfortable in a fast-paced, ever-evolving scale-up environment where roles stretch, priorities shift, and resilience matters. Believes in what Boundless Life is building for families.

What's next?

  • First call with our Recruiter (30 min)
  • Interview with the Head of Real Estate (60 min)
  • Final call with the Hiring Manager (60 min)

The process might change slightly as we go along - we’ll keep you posted at all times.

Want to know more about working at Boundless Life? Check out our story!

jobs.excerpt: Digital PR Lead at Blue ArrayLead a growing team and shape the future of Digital PR at Blue Array 🚀 Are you leading a Digital PR team, or an experienced people manager ready for your next step?
jobs.description:
Digital PR Lead at Blue Array

Lead a growing team and shape the future of Digital PR at Blue Array 🚀

Are you leading a Digital PR team, or an experienced people manager ready for your next step? At Blue Array, we’re looking for a Digital PR Lead to lead our growing Digital PR team, help develop our Digital PR offering and work alongside our Head of SEO to bring Digital PR and SEO even closer together.

It’s an exciting time to join us. We’re growing, we’ve just launched our Spanish office, and this role offers real opportunities for progression and development.

About the Digital PR team

Our Digital PR team supports clients across all sectors, from finance to fashion and lifestyle. We help them earn the visibility they deserve in the press, in search and increasingly in AI search, and drive growth. We care about results, and we care just as much about the relationships behind them, with our clients, with journalists and with each other.

The team is growing, so you’ll play a big part in shaping who joins, how we work and what we offer.

What you’ll do

You’ll lead the Digital PR team day to day, help shape our Digital PR strategy and offering, and look after some of our largest accounts. Your role will include:

  • Team leadership: Lead, mentor and develop a growing Digital PR team so everyone keeps building skills and confidence. You’ll run regular 1:1s and performance reviews, give ongoing feedback, support hiring and onboarding as the team grows, and create a collaborative culture where creativity and new ideas thrive.
  • Developing our Digital PR offering: Help shape how our Digital PR service evolves, from campaign formats and outreach approaches to building brand mentions and visibility in AI search. You’ll spot opportunities for new ideas, tools and better ways of working, and bring them into the team.
  • Strategy and standards: Design and deliver Digital PR strategies that support client objectives, SEO strategy and the agency’s vision. You’ll set clear standards for campaign quality, outreach, and reporting; build best-practice processes; and ensure the team is trained on them, so every client gets a consistent, high-quality experience.
  • Working with SEO: Partner with our Head of SEO and SEO teams to align Digital PR and SEO activity, so our campaigns have maximum impact on visibility, links and key SEO metrics.
  • Key client relationships: Be the main point of contact for some of our largest clients. You’ll oversee campaign delivery, lead strategy and performance conversations, and build long-term relationships based on trust and results.
  • Media relations: Make sure the team is building high-quality, relevant media lists, and work directly with top-tier press titles to secure interviews, exclusives and standout coverage.
  • Performance and insight: Make sure client performance meets agreed KPIs. You’ll use data to show what’s working, spot where to improve and change strategy when needed. You’ll also help the team run well, including resourcing, profitability and time utilisation.
  • New business: Support the Digital PR input on new business pitches, from shaping the ideas and pitch decks to presenting in the room. You’ll find opportunities to grow the services we offer existing clients, and work with the senior leadership team on renewals and outbound new business.
  • Industry knowledge and knowledge sharing: Keep a close eye on what’s changing in media, Digital PR and search, and share it. You’ll champion high standards of work and communication (the Blue Array Way), help upskill the team and the wider agency through BA Sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops, and represent Blue Array at industry events.

Who you are

We know that great candidates don’t always tick every box. If you’re excited about this role and our mission, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t meet every single requirement.

You don’t need to be a Head of Digital PR already. This role suits someone who is leading a team now, or who has solid people-management experience and is ready for more. Some qualities and experience that will help you succeed:

  • Strong Digital PR experience, ideally in an agency, including line managing or leading a team.
  • A track record of campaigns that earn significant media coverage, quality links and audience engagement.
  • Experience contributing to new business, such as shaping pitch ideas, building pitch decks or presenting to prospective clients.
  • A people-first approach to leadership, with the ability to motivate, develop and support a diverse team.
  • Good industry knowledge and curiosity about where Digital PR is heading, including its growing role in AI search and brand visibility.
  • A strong grasp of SEO and how Digital PR supports it.
  • Confidence with Digital PR tools, platforms and media databases.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to explain complex ideas clearly.
  • A proven track record in media relations and outreach.
  • Strong analytical skills, with experience measuring campaign success through qualitative and quantitative metrics.
  • The ability to juggle priorities in a fast-paced environment and tackle challenges proactively.
  • A passion for storytelling and a keen interest in current events and digital media trends.

If you’re ready to lead, grow your career and help shape the next chapter of Digital PR at Blue Array, we’d love to talk to you!

Please note: We can only consider applicants who have the right to work in the UK and are currently based in the UK, as we are unable to offer sponsorship at this time.

Who we are

Blue Array is the UK’s most popular and largest specialist SEO agency.

We pride ourselves on doing things differently from others in our industry, providing open, honest and actionable SEO consultancy to our clients. Regular communication and insights are core to our service, and exceptional client satisfaction is the main reason we continue to grow so quickly.

We work with some of the world’s most exciting brands, such as RAC, Cannaray, Crew, Ben Sherman, WatchFinder, Penfold, Pepper Money, Help for Heroes and many more.

We’re incredibly proud to have been named European SEO Agency of the Year and UK SEO Agency of the Year in 2026. We were also named SEO Agency of the Year at the UK Digital Growth Awards 2024. In 2025, we won Best SEO Campaign with Pepper Money and Best Local Campaign with RAC at the UK Agency Awards.

We’re a certified B Corp and an accredited Living Wage Employer, and we won Best Employee Development Programme at the Company Culture Awards.

We believe in People, Planet and Profit, in that order.

Our perks and benefits

  • A competitive salary based on experience, with biannual bonus opportunities and a pension.
  • 36 days’ holiday a year, inclusive of public holidays, plus your birthday off.
  • A remote role with flexible working and regular travel to our Reading HQ and client locations, so you get the best of both.
  • The option to work overseas for up to a month each year.*
  • A Work.Life membership allowance, so you can work from any Work.Life space across the UK.
  • An open-plan, dog-friendly office in Reading.
  • Plenty of socials throughout the year, including our summer and winter parties.
  • 3 charity days a year to support causes that matter to you.
  • Cycle-to-work and electric vehicle schemes.*
  • A range of parental leave and benefits policies, including enhanced family leave and paid dependants leave.

Health and wellbeing

  • Private medical insurance.*
  • Free gym membership.*
  • An employee assistance programme to support you whenever you need it.
  • Sickness pay beyond the statutory allowance.

Personal development

  • Plenty of internal training and development opportunities to help you grow your career.
  • Free access to the Blue Array Academy.
  • A personal development budget.
  • Regular BA Sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops, so you can learn from the people around you.

*After passing probation

Be you, with us!

At Blue Array, we are all different, and that’s what makes us great! We hire talented people with different backgrounds, stories and perspectives, because it’s the right thing to do and because it makes us stronger.

We’re actively working to increase diversity in our teams and management positions. Our ambition is to create an inclusive environment where we can all be ourselves together.

Application process

Our recruitment process is designed to help us get to know you and for you to get to know us:

  1. First stage interview: a short call with our People team to learn more about you and your experience, and to tell you more about the role.
  2. Second stage interview: an in-person interview, including a more in-depth presentation task.
  3. Final stage interview: a short call with our CEO and Founder, Simon.

What’s next?

If this sounds like you, you’re on your way to joining a forward-thinking industry leader and a team of talented, like-minded people. Simply send us your CV, and we’ll be in touch.

To find out how we use your data for recruitment, please visit .

We have a strict no-recruitment-agencies policy.

Account Executive US (Remote)

Client:
Full-time | Competitive Base + Commission

About the Role

Precoro is a leading global procurement and spend management platform trusted by over 1,000 companies across more than 80 countries. We've spent over a decade building a profitable, product-driven business across Europe, and for the past 5 years, we've been growing our presence in the U.S.

Now, we're expanding our U.S. sales team to accelerate that growth.

We're hiring a full-cycle Account Executive with a proper hunter mindset. You'll join a small, growing, high-performing AE team supported by U.S.-based SDRs and inbound demand from our Marketing team. You'll take ownership of the full sales process from outbound prospecting to closing across SMB and mid-market segments.

This is an ideal role for someone who thrives in outbound sales, desires autonomy in managing the pipeline, and is eager to contribute to shaping our U.S. go-to-market strategy.

Why Join Precoro

  • Sell a Proven Product: A mature, reliable platform trusted by finance and procurement teams globally.

  • Outbound + Inbound Support Work closely with SDRs and Marketing to build a pipeline and close deals.

  • Diverse Deal Flow Close inbound deals and outbound deals.

  • High Impact, High Autonomy Own your pipeline end-to-end and influence how we win in the U.S. market.

  • Growth Trajectory: Clear path to grow with us as we scale the U.S. team.

  • Remote-First Work from anywhere in the U.S. with performance-driven flexibility.

What You'll Do

  • Qualify and close inbound leads from demo requests and trials.

  • Build and convert outbound pipeline with SDR support.

  • Source your opportunities when needed via cold calling, email, LinkedIn, and creative outreach.

  • Run discovery calls, deliver tailored product demos, and create ROI-driven proposals.

  • Manage full sales cycles: discovery, demo, negotiation, and close.

  • Sell to Finance, Procurement, and Operations leaders, Director, VP, and C-level.

  • Maintain accurate pipeline forecasting and CRM hygiene (HubSpot or Salesforce).

  • Share insights from the field to refine our sales playbook and GTM strategy.

What Were Looking For

  • 3+ years of SaaS closing experience in a quota-carrying role.

  • Proven hunter mindset, you thrive on creating opportunities, not just working inbound.

  • Strong cold calling and outbound prospecting experience is essential.

  • Comfortable taking ownership of outbound pipeline generation alongside SDRs.

  • Consistent performance hitting or exceeding quota, with closed-won deals in the ~$50k ACV range.

  • Strong discovery, storytelling, and closing skills with VP/C-level stakeholders.

  • Attention to detail in pipeline management, forecasting, and CRM usage (HubSpot or Salesforce).

  • Self-motivated, goal-oriented, and eager to grow within a fast-paced sales environment.

jobs.description:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

Open Role: Marketing Associate

Marketers at Canonical are brand stewards and demand creators.They transform complex open-source technology into messages, stories and strategies that shape the market understanding of our vision. Some focus on differentiated product and portfolio positioning; others specialize in account-based engagement, partner and alliance messaging, or product-led growth. Whatever their specialization, each marketer works as part of a cross-functional unit, contributing campaigns and insights that help the company learn and grow faster.

We have a bias for action, focus efforts on the most impactful activities and take ownership of our results. We work across long buying cycles, balance storytelling with data, design experiments, track outcomes, and iterate rapidly to find what works.

Marketers at Canonical don’t just promote open source; they amplify it, ensuring our innovations reach the right people, at the right time, with clarity and purpose from developers to decision makers.

As a Marketing Associate , you won't just be watching from the sidelines; you will be hands-on from day one, collaborating with cross-functional teams to translate complex technical innovations into compelling market value.

Location:This role will be based remote globally

What your day will look like

  • GTM Support: Contribute to go-to-market planning and execution.

  • Storytelling: Draft and edit compelling messaging and positioning that highlights business value for diverse target audiences.

  • Campaign Coordination: Assist in developing campaign plans and content dissemination strategies to ensure our message reaches the right people.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with other demand generation and digital teams to help optimize marketing funnels and track campaign performance.

  • Event & Social Support: Work with the wider marketing team to coordinate webinars, events, and social media promotions.

What we are looking for in you

  • Tech Curiosity: A genuine passion for technology and a desire to learn about open source.

  • Analytical Thinking: An ability to break down complex issues and translate them into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Collaboration: Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships within a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

  • Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills; you enjoy storytelling and creating impactful content.

  • Proactive Mindset: A self-starter who can prioritize tasks effectively and meet deadlines in a dynamic setting.

  • Foundational Knowledge: A basic understanding of marketing principles or go-to-market strategies (via your degree, internships, or personal projects).

  • Growth Mindset: Someone who is eager to learn, open to feedback, and not afraid to take on new challenges.

What we offer you

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce.

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, please ask your Talent Partner.

  • Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!
  • Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Parental Leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’
  • Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

jobs.excerpt: Aerodynamics Expert (MSc.  or PhD)Location: Global, fully remote Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week) Schedule: Flexible—you can choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired We are looking for a highly skilled Aerodynamics Expert to contribute to an AI training project involving computational fluid dynamics, aerodynamic analysis, engineering simulation, and Python.
jobs.description:
Aerodynamics Expert (MSc. or PhD)

Location: Global, fully remote

Job Type: Contractor (~15 hours per week)

Schedule: Flexible—you can choose the hours and days you work, including weekends if desired

We are looking for a highly skilled Aerodynamics Expert to contribute to an AI training project involving computational fluid dynamics, aerodynamic analysis, engineering simulation, and Python.

The work involves creating, solving, reviewing, and validating engineering tasks that can be completed through programmatic, command-line-based workflows. A representative task may require analyzing an airfoil, preparing a computational domain and mesh, defining appropriate boundary conditions, running a CFD simulation, calculating lift and drag, and determining whether the resulting flow field is numerically and physically valid.

Required Skills

  • Python

  • Aerodynamics

What You’ll Work On

  • Solve and validate aerodynamic and fluid-dynamics problems.

  • Translate physical requirements into computational models and solver-ready cases.

  • Create or modify geometries, computational domains, and meshes.

  • Define appropriate initial conditions, boundary conditions, fluid properties, and solver settings.

  • Run CFD and aerodynamic-analysis workflows using command-line-accessible tools.

  • Use Python to automate preprocessing, simulation execution, parameter sweeps, postprocessing, and validation.

Required Qualifications

  • An MS or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, or Mechanical Engineering with an aerodynamics, fluid dynamics, or thermofluids specialization; or

  • A BS in Aerospace or Mechanical Engineering plus at least 1–2 years of aero-specific professional or research experience.

  • Strong understanding of fluid mechanics and applied aerodynamics.

  • Experience formulating and executing CFD or aerodynamic analyses.

  • Practical proficiency with Python.

  • Experience with at least one engineering tool or library that can be operated through a CLI, scripting interface, configuration files, or programmatic API.

  • Ability to select and justify modeling assumptions, boundary conditions, mesh strategies, and solver settings.

  • Ability to diagnose non-convergence, unstable solutions, incorrect results, and physically invalid outputs.

  • Ability to communicate technical reasoning and engineering trade-offs clearly.

  • Relevant tools may include Python, OpenFOAM, SU2, Gmsh, FEniCSx, Elmer, CalculiX, SciPy, or similar programmatic engineering software. Experience with an equivalent CLI-accessible tool is acceptable.

  • Relevant Python tools may include NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Matplotlib, Jupyter, solver APIs, mesh-processing libraries, or domain-specific scientific packages. No single library is mandatory.

Process

  • Apply to the role and complete the screening questions.

  • Complete an AI interview of approximately 30 minutes.

  • Complete the hiring manager review.

Compensation Structure

  • Compensation is output-based. Experts are paid per task that meets the project specifications. The time required to complete each task may vary depending on the expert’s experience and workflow.

  • Minimum submission requirements apply.

Start Timeline & Availability

We typically fill roles within 48 hours and are looking for experts who are ready to begin immediately. If selected, you will be expected to start your first task within 24–48 hours of completing onboarding.

jobs.excerpt: CD PROJEKT RED recherche un Chef d'équipe de programmation - Quêtes (Lead Quest Programmer) pour se joindre à l'équipe responsable de Cyberpunk 2, la suite de Cyberpunk 2077 et le prochain titre majeur de la franchise Cyberpunk, développé sous la direction de notre équipe nord-américaine établie à Boston.
jobs.description:
CD PROJEKT RED recherche un Chef d'équipe de programmation - Quêtes (Lead Quest Programmer) pour se joindre à l'équipe responsable de Cyberpunk 2, la suite de Cyberpunk 2077 et le prochain titre majeur de la franchise Cyberpunk, développé sous la direction de notre équipe nord-américaine établie à Boston.

Il s'agit d'un rôle clé au sein du projet, consistant à diriger l'équipe d’ingénieurs axée sur les technologies narratives pour Cyberpunk 2. Notre système narratif joue un rôle central dans la concrétisation d'expériences riches et immersives. Dans ce rôle, vous servirez d’intermédiaire entre la vision créative et l'exécution technique, en travaillant en étroite collaboration avec les créateurs de contenu narratif, les responsables de quêtes, les directeurs ainsi que les architectes principaux et responsables principaux de la maintenance de notre système narratif sur mesure et partagé. Ensemble, vous veillerez à ce que nos outils et flux de travaux offrent aux créateurs la flexibilité et le soutien nécessaires pour créer des expériences narratives captivantes.

Responsabilités quotidiennes :

Gestion des personnes et gestion d'équipe :

  • Gérer les membres de votre équipe directe et soutenir leur développement professionnel ainsi que leurs ambitions de carrière.
  • Mener régulièrement des rencontres individuelles (1:1), des évaluations de rendement, ainsi que gérer le processus de recrutement et les plans de promotion.
  • Guider et encadrer votre équipe d’ingénieurs concernant la qualité du code, l'efficacité des flux de travaux collaboratifs et l'exécution technique.

Mener le développement des systèmes et des outils :

  • Travailler directement avec les concepteurs de quêtes (créateurs de contenu et chefs d'équipe) et les directeurs afin de traduire les exigences créatives et narratives en besoins techniques clairs.
  • Collaborer avec les architectes principaux et responsables principaux de la maintenance de notre système de quêtes sur mesure et partagé, afin de formuler les demandes de fonctionnalités, d'en assurer l'intégration et de veiller à leur amélioration continue entre les projets.
  • Mener le développement, l'intégration et l'évolution des fonctionnalités de quêtes pour notre projet, en veillant à ce que le travail d'ingénierie requis soit mis en œuvre et livré de manière efficace.
  • Veiller à ce que les outils de quêtes fonctionnent de manière efficace sans pour autant compromettre la performance du temps d’exécution, garantissant des flux de travaux itératifs fluides pour les créateurs de contenu.
  • Assurer la maintenance et l’optimisation des fonctionnalités narratives et de quêtes, en s’assurant de leur intégration harmonieuse avec les autres composantes du jeu.

Exécution et collaboration en technologies partagées :

  • Favoriser les flux de travaux collaboratifs et éprouvés avec des équipes qui partagent leurs technologies tout en travaillant sur plusieurs projets.
  • Écrire du code C++ de haute qualité, propre, optimisé et dont il est facile d’assurer la maintenance.
  • Rechercher, diagnostiquer et résoudre les bogues au sein des fonctionnalités de quêtes et des outils auteur.
  • Travailler en collaboration avec les équipes chargées des cinématiques, du récit et de la jouabilité centrale (core gameplay) pour veiller à l'intégration parfaite des systèmes de quêtes dans toutes les composantes du jeu.
  • Avoir au moins 7 ans d'expérience professionnelle en programmation dans l'industrie du jeu vidéo AAA.
  • Avoir au moins 1 an d'expérience dans le leadership technique, dans la gestion de personnel ou à la tête d'une équipe d'ingénieurs.
  • Avoir une excellente maîtrise de la programmation en C++.
  • Pouvoir démontrer avoir de l’expérience dans le développement de systèmes de quêtes personnalisés, d'outils narratifs personnalisés ou de flux de travaux pour un éditeur dont le fonctionnement repose sur des nœuds (node-based editor).
  • Pouvoir démontrer avoir travaillé au sein d'un environnement hautement collaboratif de technologies partagées, couvrant plusieurs équipes ou projets.
  • Être capable de cerner les besoins des membres des équipes plus créatives que techniques, et de traduire la vision de leurs concepts en exigences techniques claires.
  • Avoir d’excellentes compétences en communication et en travail collaboratif pour pouvoir travailler efficacement dans des environnements multiculturels et sur plusieurs fuseaux horaires.

Compétences optionnelles recherchées :
(veuillez noter que ces compétences ne sont pas obligatoires pour postuler)

  • Avoir une connaissance de l'architecture d'Unreal Engine.
  • Avoir une compréhension de l’architecture d’un réseau multijoueur et de la synchronisation client-serveur pour l'état du jeu et les quêtes.
  • Avoir participé au développement et au lancement d'au moins un jeu AAA utilisant des outils narratifs ou de quêtes sur mesure ou personnalisés.
  • Avoir une connaissance des outils d'interface utilisateur d'Unreal Engine ou de la création de scripts d'édition pour des outils de contenu personnalisés.

Vous avez jusqu’au 15 décembre 2026 pour envoyer votre candidature pour ce poste.

Ce poste peut être pourvu entièrement en télétravail depuis le Canada.

Santé et bien-être

  • Assurance maladie prise en charge par l'employeur (soins dentaires, de la vue et santé mentale).
  • Soutien gratuit en santé mentale, incluant l'accès à des services de consultation, des soins psychiatriques et une variété de webinaires sur le bien-être.
  • Congés payés : 26 jours de vacances, 10 jours de congé maladie et 12 jours fériés par année.
  • REER collectif avec cotisation équivalente de l'employeur.
  • Compte de dépenses lié au style de vie (LSA) : 100 $ CAD par mois applicables pour l’exercice physique, le bien-être, les frais d'Internet, l'équipement de télétravail, la formation, les services de diffusion en continu (streaming), et plus encore.
  • Congé menstruel : les personnes qui ont leurs règles peuvent prendre un jour de congé supplémentaire en cas de douleurs menstruelles.
  • Réseau RED Parents : soutien offert aux parents qui travaillent.
  • Horaires de travail flexibles.

Avantages et développement professionnel

  • Formations, séminaires et cours : des ateliers de travail en interne, des initiatives pour le partage des connaissances, des didacticiels en ligne et des cours via e-learning sont disponibles.
  • Un kit de bienvenue rempli de cadeaux : pour vous aider à vous sentir rapidement chez vous dès votre arrivée.
  • Un environnement de travail véritablement international : vous aurez l’opportunité de faire la connaissance de personnes diverses venant des quatre coins du monde, et de travailler avec elles.
  • Aucun code vestimentaire : nous privilégions une ambiance décontractée.

Ce poste est à pourvoir dans le cadre d'un remplacement.

Échelle salariale annuelle estimée pour ce poste : 180 100 $ CAD à 247 600 $ CAD

Ce poste peut également donner droit à des options d'achat d'actions discrétionnaires.

Chez CD PROJEKT RED, la rémunération globale pour nos postes en Amérique du Nord est établie selon les données concurrentielles du marché, la localisation géographique et des facteurs individuels liés aux besoins de l'entreprise. L'échelle salariale de base est sujette à changement et pourrait être modifiée à l'avenir. Les offres finales sont déterminées en fonction de facteurs liés à l'emploi, tels que l'expérience, les qualifications et le lieu de travail.

Si vous avez constaté des irrégularités (par exemple des violations légales ou éthiques) au cours de notre processus de recrutement, veuillez cliquer ici pour les signaler de façon anonyme.

Notre mission : créer des jeux de rôle narratifs révolutionnaires qui parlent au cœur des joueurs. Souhaitez-vous en savoir davantage sur notre culture d’entreprise ? Nous vous invitons à nous voir sur les réseaux sociaux et à vous rendre sur notre chaîne YouTube et notre blog Beyond the Game où des membres de nos équipes vous font directement part d’anecdotes et d’idées provenant de l’envers du décor!

jobs.title: Director, Newborn Health
jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Program Overview

Each year, approximately 2.3 million newborns die globally, and an additional 1.9 million babies are stillborn. More than half of neonatal deaths occur in sub-Saharan Africa, where newborns face roughly a ten-fold higher risk of death than those born in high-income countries. Prematurity, birth asphyxia, neonatal infections, and preventable maternal infections in pregnancy together account for the vast majority of these deaths and adverse outcomes. The tragedy is not a lack of solutions. Proven, cost-effective interventions exist across this continuum — the barriers are policy, system, supply, and workforce gaps that keep effective care from reaching mothers and babies at the moments that matter most.

CHAI’s Women and Newborn Health (WNH) cluster is working to close those gaps. Across more than 15 countries in sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia, our country teams and global team work with governments to ensure that newborns and their mothers can access the commodities, clinical care, and health system support they need to survive and thrive. Our newborn health portfolio encompasses work on preterm respiratory care, congenital syphilis elimination, and country-led initiatives addressing other drivers of newborn mortality and morbidity — with an ambition to grow into a comprehensive, evidence-driven newborn health program over the coming years. Our strategy focuses on areas where CHAI has distinctive value to add — through market shaping, commodity access, clinical quality improvement, health systems strengthening, and the translation of global evidence into government-owned programs at scale.

The Director, Newborn Health will lead this agenda. This is one of the most consequential roles in the WNH cluster, requiring someone who can operate at the intersection of clinical and technical depth, strategic leadership, and hands-on execution — and who is motivated by the opportunity to shape CHAI’s contribution to reducing preventable newborn deaths and stillbirths at scale.

This is a team that is building, not maintaining. The Director will inherit strong foundations and will be expected to accelerate progress, expand scope, and position CHAI as a leading contributor to global efforts to reduce neonatal mortality and preventable stillbirths.

Role Overview

We are looking for a Director who will serve as CHAI’s global newborn health lead, with primary accountability for the existing preterm respiratory care and congenital syphilis elimination workstreams and a mandate to develop the strategy and support fundraising for a comprehensive newborn health portfolio over time. The right candidate will combine genuine technical depth in newborn or maternal health with the strategic and managerial capability to lead a complex, multi-country program.

The Director will own programmatic outcomes — working with country teams to drive measurable improvements in clinical quality and commodity access, while engaging actively in global partner networks, influencing the sector, and building the evidence and relationships needed to expand CHAI’s neonatal ambition.

The Director will manage a team of program staff, report to the VP for Women’s and Newborn Health, and work closely with other WNH leads across maternal health, commodity security and financing, and AI-enabled diagnostics, as well as with CHAI’s market shaping team, M&E/research colleagues, and country-based staff across Africa and Southeast Asia.

Responsibilities

Set Strategy

  • Build a programmatic vision that extends beyond current workstreams to address the leading drivers of neonatal death comprehensively, and that positions CHAI for impact at scale across its program countries.
  • In line with this vision, define and evolve CHAI’s global newborn health strategy, in close collaboration with the WNH VP, country teams, and key partners — determining priorities across the newborn mortality continuum, sequencing investments, and identifying where CHAI adds the most distinctive value.
  • Provide strategic leadership and technical direction for the existing preterm respiratory care and congenital syphilis elimination workstreams, while supporting country-led initiatives in other areas of newborn health.
  • Work with country teams to identify entry points for portfolio expansion into new areas, including birth asphyxia and neonatal infections, building the evidence base and partnerships needed to move from opportunity identification to funded programs.
  • Stay at the frontier of newborn health; bring relevant clinical, epidemiological, market, and programmatic insights into CHAI’s strategy.
  • Treat strategy as a living document: build in regular review points and adjust course decisively based on evidence and evolving conditions.Execute Programs and Support Country Teams.
  • Lead execution of global newborn health workstreams, ensuring technical quality, country relevance, and measurable impact across the portfolio.
  • Provide hands-on technical support to country teams across program areas, including on clinical intervention roll-out, commodity access, government procurement planning, provider training, health information system strengthening, and demand-side programming.
  • Support country-led newborn health work across a range of program areas by providing thought partnership, technical resources, and connections to global evidence and partner networks.
  • Provide strategic direction to inform market shaping activities for key newborn commodities and diagnostics, collaborating closely with CHAI’s market shaping team and external partners.
  • Oversee the development, validation, and application of impact models and cost-effectiveness analyses to support program prioritization, funder engagement, and government decision-making.
  • Identify and develop new programmatic opportunities across the newborn health portfolio, moving from landscape analysis to actionable strategy and resource mobilization.

Stakeholder Engagement and Sector Influence

  • Build and sustain trusted relationships with key stakeholders across the newborn health landscape, including WHO, bilateral and multilateral partners, implementing organizations, academic institutions, and national governments.
  • Represent CHAI in global fora on newborn health, congenital syphilis elimination, and related areas, contributing to how the sector prioritizes resources and approaches these challenges.
  • Actively contribute to relevant WHO technical processes and working groups, providing market data, programmatic evidence, and technical coordination.
  • Coordinate with partner organizations to align strategies, share learning, and build a coherent ecosystem of support for country programs.Resource Mobilization and Donor Management.
  • Engage funders to ensure the newborn health portfolio is appropriately and sustainably resourced, developing high-quality concept notes and proposals across a diverse set of prospective and current donors.
  • Manage relevant grant components, ensuring high-quality reporting, proactive risk management, and disciplined use of resources.
  • Identify and cultivate new funding opportunities as CHAI’s newborn health program expands in scope and ambition.

Team Leadership and Organizational Collaboration

  • Manage and develop a team of program staff, providing strategic direction, technical guidance, and meaningful investment in professional growth.
  • Work in close partnership with other WNH team leads to ensure coherence across the cluster portfolio, including where newborn health intersects with maternal health, commodity security and financing, and AI-enabled diagnostics.
  • Collaborate with CHAI’s market shaping team, M&E/research colleagues, and country-based staff, recognizing that durable global strategies are built on the insights and relationships that country teams bring.
  • Contribute to WNH team culture, operations, and organizational initiatives including Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in public health, medicine, or a related field.
  • Ten or more years of progressive experience in global health, with demonstrated deepening of responsibility over time; substantive experience in maternal or newborn health, or in adjacent areas such as diagnostic or commodity access programs.
  • In-depth understanding of the newborn health landscape, including leading causes of neonatal mortality and morbidity, the evidence base for key interventions, and the health system and supply chain conditions that determine whether those interventions reach babies at scale.
  • Experience with cost-effectiveness analysis, impact modelling, or other quantitative approaches to program prioritization and investment case development.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategy in complex, multi-country environments — translating high-level goals into actionable plans, sequencing investments across competing priorities, and adjusting course as conditions evolve.
  • Proven experience engaging with and influencing multilateral organizations, bilateral donors, and global health partners.
  • Strong analytical skills and ability to engage rigorously with epidemiological, programmatic, and market data to support decision-making.
  • Excellent communicator, able to distil complex clinical and programmatic information into clear, compelling narratives for diverse audiences, from Ministry of Health counterparts to senior funders.
  • Proven track record of managing and developing teams in a matrixed, multicultural environment.
  • Strong work ethic, integrity, credibility, and dedication to CHAI’s mission.
  • Fluency in English required; French is a significant asset given CHAI’s program footprint.

Advantages

  • Experience living and working in sub-Saharan Africa.
  • Technical expertise in one or more areas of newborn health, including preterm care, neonatal infections, birth asphyxia, or maternal infections with newborn consequences.
  • Experience working on sexually transmitted infection programs, eMTCT, or triple elimination, including familiarity with the WHO Triple Elimination agenda and its country-level implementation.
  • Experience with market shaping, commodity access, or health commodity procurement in LMICs.
  • Experience developing investment cases or enabling environment strategies for diagnostic or therapeutic product introduction.
  • Experience working with WHO technical working groups or contributing to global guideline development processes.
  • Demonstrated success in fundraising from major donor organizations, including developing and winning competitive proposals.
  • Experience building out a new or expanding programmatic area — identifying entry points, building strategy, and mobilizing the resources needed for growth.
  • Experience working remotely with a geographically dispersed team.

Attributes

  • Deeply mission-driven: motivated by the prospect of substantially reducing neonatal deaths and stillbirths through interventions that already exist, and by the opportunity to build the programmatic infrastructure that makes that possible at scale.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset: energized by building, creating, and embracing innovative approaches.
  • Execution-focused, with a bias for moving from analysis to action and a track record of turning strategy into results.
  • Strategically adaptive: able to hold a long-term vision while adjusting tactics as the clinical, programmatic, and funding landscape evolves.
  • Comfortable making directional calls in the face of uncertainty.
  • CHAI fit: collaborative, analytically rigorous, grounded in country realities, and committed to government ownership and sustainable impact over the long term. Possess humility and integrity.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence: builds trust across diverse cultural contexts, institutional settings, and stakeholder groups.
  • Comfortable with breadth and complexity: this role spans neonatal clinical care, market dynamics, government systems, global partner coordination, and fundraising — and requires someone who thrives at that intersection.
  • Willingness to travel approximately 25-35% of the year to program countries and global convenings.

Real ownership from day one, not check-ins and micromanagement. That's what the Business Development Representative role at Nortal looks like.

What working with us looks like

  • Remote work with a LATAM team. Coffee breaks, tech talks, and games keep it human, even at a distance.

  • Support beyond the job. Our People Care team helps with time off, wellness, and anything in between.

What you get

  • National holidays.
  • Sick leave, no stress attached.
  • A yearly refundable credit. Spend it on anything related to your health and well-being.
  • A day off for your birthday.

About this search

Great talent doesn't wait for job postings, so we don't either. We're building a network of skilled professionals for roles that come up regularly with our clients.

Join our Future Talent network and you'll be one of the first people we reach when the right opening appears. We make around 160 hires a year, so it happens often.

The role

As a Business Development Representative, you will think like an account-based marketer. You'll design and run the strategy to attract new opportunities and relevant connections for Nortal, with a clear target of opportunities detected each period.

You'll spend as much time designing and testing ABM plays as you do on outreach, and you'll own the results from first touch to handoff to our new business team..

Your day-to-day:

Design the attraction strategy

  • Design and execute the strategy to attract new opportunities and build relevant connections for Nortal in the US.
  • Build and maintain a tiered target account list (one-to-one, one-to-few, one-to-many) with sales leadership.
  • Research each priority account: business priorities, tech stack, recent triggers such as funding, leadership changes, or modernization programs, and the buying committee.

Run ABM campaigns that convert

  • Turn account research into campaign concepts with a clear message, offer, and call to action for each person.
  • Write the copy and launch the campaign: email sequences, LinkedIn content, landing pages, direct mail, and event invitations.
  • Coordinate plays across email, LinkedIn, paid social, intent-based advertising, webinars, and events, so sales and marketing hit each account with one story.

Generate and qualify opportunities

  • Hit your target of opportunities detected and qualified.
  • Prospect into VP, C-level, and senior IT and digital leaders at mid-market and enterprise companies.
  • Book discovery meetings, qualify them against our criteria, and hand them over with full context.
  • Keep the CRM clean so anyone can see where every account stands.

Test and Challenge

  • Try new channels, messages, and formats, and challenge the way we do things today.
  • Run A/B tests on messages, offers, and channels, and report what worked and what didn't.
  • Share what you learn so the next play starts smarter.

What we're looking for

  • 3+ Years in business development, SDR/BDR, or demand generation roles, with at least two in IT services, software engineering services, or digital consulting.
  • Strong, hands-on experience designing and running ABM campaigns. You can walk us through one you built, the accounts it targeted, and what it produced.
  • A track record of booking meetings with senior buyers at US enterprises.
  • A test-and-learn mindset: you try new things, question what isn't working, and bring ideas backed by data.
  • Enough technical fluency to talk credibly about cloud, data, AI, software development, and nearshore delivery.
  • Comfort with numbers: you track your funnel, know your conversion rates, and change course when the data says so.
  • Advanced English Level is required for this role, as you will work with US clients. Effective communication in English is essential to deliver the best solutions to our clients and expand your horizons. 

How the process works

  1. Apply and upload your resume.
  1. We review your profile and add it to our talent database.
  1. We reach out for an interview to learn about your experience and share more about what we're looking for.
  1. When a role opens that fits, we contact you to start the process. Because we already know you, it moves faster.
  1. No intermediaries. You deal with us directly.

About Nortal

For over 25 years, we've built the systems that global enterprises and public institutions run on. Today, that means using AI and data to help organizations make better decisions, not just build what they asked for.

We believe good solutions don't have to be complicated. That's why our clients trust us with the initiatives that matter most.

Real ownership, real impact, no micromanagement. If that's what you're after, apply now. 👇

jobs.description:
Langate is an award-winning provider of web development services in 3 main categories: business, healthcare, and education. At Langate, we're passionate about crafting digital solutions that make a real impact. We take immense pride in our strong collaboration with the U.S. We're here to shape the future of technology, one milestone at a time.

In addition to technical expertise, we value excellent communication skills. Collaboration and effective teamwork are the cornerstones of our success, and we believe in fostering an environment where everyone’s voice is heard and valued.

We are looking for a hands-on AI Engineering Lead who combines software architecture, team leadership, and practical AI engineering. This is a role for someone who can quickly understand a complex existing system, define where it should go next, and lead a team to get there, while keeping the live product stable for its users.

About the project 

The product is a SaaS platform for the U.S. healthcare insurance domain. It helps customers read, collect, and process large volumes of insurance-related data and connects to multiple data sources in different ways. It is a multi-tier system with data warehouse, middleware, and front-end layers, built on the .NET stack (ASP.NET MVC and Web API, message queuing, Windows services, and a set of microservices) with MS SQL. The product is live and in active use, and the company is now preparing its next stage: modernizing the platform and bringing an AI-driven approach to architecture and development so that new functionality reaches users faster. Which parts move to a new architecture, which new services are built with an AI-driven approach, and what stays as it is are exactly the decisions this role will help shape.

What success looks like: in your first two months you get to know the system and the team, shape the first version of the target architecture together with our Engineering Manager, and present a small proof of concept. By month three, the goal is an agreed plan, development running at a steady pace, and first practical results on one to three new modules or features. By month six, the new team is delivering new functionality on the agreed architecture.

Requirements:

  • Proven experience as a Software / Application or Solution Architect, combined with a Team Lead role

  • Strong .NET / C# background across ASP.NET Framework and ASP.NET Core, including migration from .NET Framework to modern .NET

  • Hands-on front-end experience with Angular and React: the current front end is built on Angular, and React is a likely direction for new modules given its strong support in AI-driven and agentic development

  • Practical experience designing and running solutions on Azure Cloud: Web Apps, Azure Container Apps, Service Bus, Key Vault, networking (VNets, private endpoints), Cosmos DB and Application Insights

  • Hands-on experience modernizing brownfield or legacy systems: auditing an existing system, defining a target architecture, writing specifications, and planning a phased migration

  • Mature architecture practice: documenting decisions as ADRs, defining and measuring non-functional requirements (performance, scalability, availability, security, observability), and explaining trade-offs to technical and business stakeholders

  • Around 1+ year of practical AI Engineering (AI SDLC / Agentic Engineering) experience: spec-driven development, agentic coding tools, context engineering, AI-assisted review and testing, and readiness to write code yourself, not only to lead

  • Strong quality engineering mindset: test strategy, automated testing and CI/CD quality gates, especially for AI-generated code

  • Experience teaching and coaching engineers in AI-driven development through workshops, pairing and hands-on examples, and turning individual practices into team standards

  • Experience across several projects and different architectures, not just one system

  • Experience managing an engineering team and introducing AI-driven approaches into delivery

Nice to have:

  • Experience in the healthcare or insurance domain (HIPAA, working with sensitive data)

  • Experience in a product company or a startup, or your own side project or business

  • Experience building AI capabilities into products (LLM integration, RAG, evaluations)

  • Ability to move fast with lean processes and a clear focus on business results

Responsibilities:

  • Go through knowledge transfer and build a deep understanding of the existing product, its architecture and integrations

  • Define and agree on non-functional requirements with the Engineering Manager and the business, and use them as the basis for architecture decisions

  • Definethetargetarchitectureand a phasedmodernizationstrategy: whattorewrite, whattokeep (includingintegrations) andwhattomoveintoseparateservices

  • Record key decisions as ADRs, turn them into clear architecture artifacts and specifications, and validate them together with the Engineering Manager

  • Build a proofofconcept, thenleadtheimplementationofnewmodulesandfeatureswhilestayinghands-oninthecode

  • Act as Team Lead: own the team’s technical delivery, run design and code reviews, and grow engineers through mentoring and pairing

  • Teach the team AI-SDLC and Agentic Engineering through regular workshops and work on real tasks, and maintain a shared team playbook (specs, agent instructions, review checklists)

  • Assessthecurrentteam, formthenewcoreteam,andbuildtrustandeffectivecollaborationwithinit

  • Makesurethecurrentproductstaysstableinproductionthroughoutthetransition

  

We offer:

  • Real influence on the architectural future of the product, with end-to-end ownership from strategy and PoC to production

  • A hiring process without a take-home assignment

  • 20 days of paid vacation and paid sick leave

  • Official Ukrainian holidays are non-working days

  • Free English lessons

  • Paid courses and certifications

  • Coach/psychologist consultation

  • Workshops

  • Career development plan

  • Mentoring Education

  • Medical Health Insurance

Schedule: 5/2, full-time, approximately 11:00–19:00 Kyiv time. Occasional meetings may run until 19:00–20:00 because of collaboration with the team in the U.S. Daily team meeting at 15:00 Kyiv time.

Why Choose Us? What Do We Offer that's Exceptional?

  1. Cutting-Edge Technologies on Real Projects: At Langate, you'll work with modern technologies on live projects and have room to introduce new approaches and tools.

  1. Work-Life Balance with Benefits: We value work-life balance and offer paid time off, including vacation days and sick leave.

  1. Investment in Your Growth: We're committed to your professional development. You can expect training programs, courses, and opportunities to enhance your English language skills.

  1. Team Building and Unity: We know that a happy team is a productive team. That's why we organize team-building events and group activities to foster strong bonds and a sense of belonging.

When you choose us, you're choosing a company that values innovation, invests in its employees, and provides a supportive and engaging work environment. Join us in shaping the future of technology!

jobs.description:
Location: Flexible within the US

Type: Full-time

Team: HR and Talent

Job level: LSS5 - Vice President

Start date: January 2027

Priority Application Review Deadline: November 6, 2026

About Us

Relay Graduate School of Education (Relay) is an accredited not-for-profit institution of higher education serving thousands of educators from across the country, from pre-service teachers to system-level leaders. Relay is integrating with Teaching Lab, a leading national education non-profit providing teacher and leader coaching. Together, Relay and Teaching Lab help school system partners build coherent systems that support educators throughout their educator journey, from a first-year teacher finding their footing to experienced instructional, school, and system leaders. By bringing together the talent, infrastructure, and institutional knowledge of both organizations, we will strengthen our collective ability to help educators learn, grow, and lead—so that all students have the opportunity to thrive.

Summary of Position

The Vice President, HR and Talent owns the organization's HR and Talent department, running consistent processes, governing accurate and accessible people data, and acting as a strategic partner that helps leaders, managers, and team members navigate their own people decisions. This role owns the vision for HR and Talent across four functional pillars: Talent Attraction & Acquisition, People Operations & Compliance, Compensation & Benefits, and Business Partnership & Employee Relations. As Relay and Teaching Lab integrate, the VP owns the HR and Talent aspects of integration, ensuring one coherent people function across the combined organization. This role shapes organization-wide strategy and resolves cross-departmental tradeoffs on workforce planning, organizational design, and compensation, in partnership with the Chief Operating Officer and the Executive Team. The VP is accountable for the performance, sustainability, and results of the HR and Talent department.

Essential Projects, Duties, and Responsibilities:

Specifically, the Vice President, HR and Talent will hold responsibilities in the following functional areas:

Own HR and Talent Department Strategy & Integration

  • Own the vision and multi-year strategy for the HR and Talent department, spanning Talent Attraction & Acquisition, People Operations & Compliance, Compensation & Benefits, and Business Partnership & Employee Relations
  • Own the HR aspects of the Relay/Teaching Lab integration, ensuring one coherent people function, policy set, and system of record across the combined organization
  • Shape organization-wide strategy and resolve cross-departmental tradeoffs on workforce planning, organizational design, and compensation, in partnership with the COO and the Executive Team
  • Hold accountability for the performance, sustainability, and results of the HR and Talent department, including whether team members experience HR and Talent as a responsive and trusted resource

Compensation & Benefits Strategy

  • Own compensation philosophy, job architecture, and pay equity practices, ensuring fair and consistent pay across the organization
  • Own total rewards strategy in partnership with the Executive Team, designing direct and indirect compensation programs that fairly pay employees and contractors
  • Oversee benefits design, eligibility, and ACA compliance, and oversee management of compensation and benefits vendors and data accuracy

Talent Attraction & Acquisition Strategy

  • Set the vision and strategic direction for talent acquisition, ensuring recruitment priorities align with organizational goals, evolving workforce needs, and long-term talent requirements.
  • Establish an org-wide talent strategy that strengthens the organization’s ability to attract, assess, and retain high-quality talent across functions and leadership levels.
  • Shape workforce planning and talent forecasting in partnership with executive leadership, connecting organizational priorities, future capabilities, and staffing needs.
  • Define the principles, standards, and success measures that promote equitable hiring practices, a strong candidate experience, and consistent recruitment outcomes across the organization.
  • Evaluate talent acquisition effectiveness using data, market insights, and organizational outcomes to inform strategic decisions and continuous improvement.

People Operations & Compliance Strategy

  • Set the vision and strategic direction for people policies and the employee/contractor handbook, ensuring they are current, legally compliant, and clearly communicated
  • Set the vision and strategic direction for people data and data integrity, ensuring the organization has one accurate system of record
  • Oversee the compliance calendar and lead efforts to manage organizational risk and comply with federal, state, and local legal requirements for a multi-state, multi-entity workforce
  • Set the vision and strategic direction for onboarding, offboarding, and Tier 1 employee support, ensuring a consistent and welcoming employee lifecycle experience
  • Oversee management of the performance review cycle end-to-end, including calibration support

Business Partnership & Employee Relations Strategy

  • Set the vision and strategic direction for how HR and Talent Business Partners serve as embedded strategic partners to function leaders on org design and workforce planning
  • Set the vision for the organization's approach to employee relations and manager coaching, ensuring issues are addressed early, and coaching measurably reduces repeat issues
  • Oversee calibration of performance conversations and ratings across teams to ensure consistency and fairness
  • In consultation with the COO, Executive Team, and General Counsel, provide guidance on the most complex employee relations, conduct, and performance matters, including investigations of alleged misconduct

People Leadership: Lead Directors and Senior Directors

  • Provide vision, direction, and oversight for direct reports and project team members
  • Model people-manager competencies that support a positive culture and high productivity, including coaching, feedback, and development planning
  • Ensure direct reports and project team members successfully achieve annual goals
  • Monitor team capacity and workload to sustain effectiveness without burnout
  • Oversee hiring for open roles within the team

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Collaborate with the Executive Team, department leaders, and team members at every level to generate ideas, strategies, and systems that meet organizational goals related to HR and Talent
  • Provide HR and Talent written updates through various reporting channels (e.g., internal newsletter, progress monitoring, Executive Team reports), incorporating metrics on progress
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for HR and Talent matters relating to organizational initiatives, policies, practices, and employee relations issues
  • Lead efforts that build inclusion and belonging for all team members, embedding this lens into HR and Talent's systems and practices

Continuous Learning

  • Stay abreast of key research and guidance in HR, talent acquisition, compensation, and employee relations; attend learning experiences to build relevant skills and competencies
  • Continuously update job knowledge through conferences, professional publications, and professional networks

Perform other duties as assigned by the Manager, Department leadership, and/or Executive Team.

Essential Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources Management, Organizational Psychology, or a related field
  • 10+ years of progressively responsible HR experience, including 5+ years at the Director level or above leading HR operations and employee programs throughout the employee lifecycle
  • 5+ years managing people, including experience managing other people managers
  • 5+ years of experience aligning and supporting business operations for a geographically dispersed, multi-entity workforce
  • 5+ years advising leaders on complex employee relations matters related to conduct and/or performance
  • Professional HR certification (e.g., PHR, SHRM-CP, or a senior-level equivalent)
  • Multi-state HR experience, with knowledge of compliance across varied jurisdictions
  • Demonstrated experience setting multi-year HR Talent strategy and building durable, scalable systems (e.g., HRIS, compensation architecture, compliance systems)
  • Demonstrated experience leading HR through a merger, acquisition, or large-scale organizational integration
  • Demonstrated ability to lead inclusion and belonging initiatives, including equitable hiring practices, pay equity audits, and employee inclusion programs, using metrics to track success
  • Advanced knowledge of and experience applying Federal and State employment law across multiple jurisdictions
  • Experience managing HR systems (HRIS/HRM) and overseeing HR systems integrations
  • Proficient with Google Suite and Microsoft Office Suite

Desirable Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, or a related field
  • Senior-level professional HR certification (e.g., SPHR, SHRM-SCP)
  • Experience in higher education or K-12 education context
  • Experience leading HR and Talent during a merger or acquisition

Compensation

Relay and Teaching Lab are committed to creating and maintaining a compensation and benefits system that supports our ability to recruit and retain a diverse and talented team. As we make decisions about compensation, we will be guided by the following values: clarity, consistency, and internal equity. The salary range for this role is $144,700 to $247,700.

Relay and Teaching Lab offer a comprehensive total rewards package. For full-time roles, this includes health insurance benefits, disability and life insurance, retirement plan, professional development, gym reimbursement, adoption assistance, paid time off (PTO), parental leave, etc.

Work Location Policy

Employees must have a primary work location within the U.S., where they are legally authorized to work.

Relay Graduate School of Education and Teaching Lab provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees.
