jobs.description:
The Center for International Environmental Law (CIEL) is a dynamic, nonprofit organization that works at the intersection of human rights and the environment. CIEL is comprised of attorneys, campaigners, researchers, and communicators who have extensive experience in leading international strategies to advance everyone’s right to a healthy environment. Many of our program areas explore innovative developments in international environmental law and human rights, including in their direct link with other international legal fields, such as international investment law or international trade law.

Our legal internship program offers a unique opportunity for law students to develop skills in the field of international environmental law, and using legal strategies to protect human rights and the environment. Learning from and supervised by a diverse staff of experts and attorneys, internships offer insight into innovative developments in international environmental law and human rights, by honing thoughtful and creative research and analysis. Offering this internship is central to CIEL’s mission of developing the next generation of environmental leaders and lawyers through real-world training and practice.

Responsibilities of a legal intern may include researching and writing about areas of domestic and international law, including environmental and human rights law, international investment law, and international trade law and policy; assisting with policy analysis and advocacy; attending meetings and conferences; assisting with the production of CIEL publications, legal opinions and legal briefs; support in the preparation of amicus curiae before international tribunals and otherwise working closely with CIEL staff on various projects. Successful applicants generally possess excellent research and writing skills and a strong dedication to public interest law

Stipend:

A monthly stipend is available for any intern eligible to receive it under the rules applied by their jurisdiction and educational institution. The basic stipend is $2,600 per month for a full-time internship in the United States. For less than full-time internships, the stipend is prorated according to the intern’s approximate level of time commitment to CIEL. Stipends are intended to make the CIEL internship more readily available to aspiring professionals, and are not intended to provide compensation, create a legal or employment relationship between the intern and CIEL, or otherwise modify the legal nature of the internship program.

Requirements:

  • Applicants should be enrolled in a course of study leading to a postgraduate law degree (JD, LLM) or similar professional qualification for the duration of the internship. We cannot accept recent graduates.
  • Applicants must possess some experience with international environmental or human rights law, either through graduate-level courses or work experience.
  • Applicants must be willing to make a ten-week commitment of 40 hours/week.

To apply, please submit your cover letter, resume, and a writing sample (please, no legal memos - see FAQ below for more information). Please not send transcripts.

Application Deadline:

  • Summer 2027 US Internship Application Deadline: Monday, March 15, 2027.

FAQ:

  • May I undertake my internship remotely? All CIEL legal internships may be carried out remotely. Please note that we can only consider applicants for this US internship who will carry out their internship while physically residing in the United States. Remote work from other countries cannot be accommodated.
  • What time period does the summer session cover? Roughly June through August, although we can be flexible regarding starting and ending dates.
  • What should I submit as a writing sample? Feel free to submit something that you feel demonstrates your writing ability. This can include undergraduate work. Please avoid 1L legal writing memos if possible.
  • May I apply to both offices? You may apply to both our Geneva and Washington, DC offices. Applying for internships with our Geneva office is a separate process, please see that application page.
  • Will CIEL sponsor a visa for me?CIEL in the United States is unable to sponsor visas. For non-US citizens, you must be a currently enrolled student in the US and would undertake your internship as part of your university-sponsored student visa.

Description

The Site Budget and Contract Lead (SBCL) leads the development of investigator budget and contract proposals. The SBCS acts as the main point of contact for budget and contract negotiations for investigator sites across North America, EU and other countries, as applicable and Sponsors. The SBCS will be responsible for all project activities related to contracts/budgets and will interact with clients, as needed. Frequent collaboration with internal and external teams is expected.

This role will be perfect for you if:

  • You can easily achieve consensus while maintaining positive working relationships with external partners.
  • Your team can count on you to get things done.
  • You have an ease to work with numbers (standardized budgets).
  • You are comfortable working under time pressure and tight timeliness

More specifically, the Site Budget and Contract Lead must:

  • Develop and maintain positive and productive relationships with clinical research sites and Sponsors.
  • Develop the draft clinical budgets for new studies.
  • Develop and maintain the country-specific, sponsor approved, minimum and maximum budget grid for negotiation with sites.
  • Develop the project-specific Clinical Trial Agreement (CTA) template for studies, customized per country-specific and sponsor requirements.
  • Facilitate the negotiation and signature of the site budgets/contracts with investigators, in collaboration with Legal Affairs, and when appropriate with Sponsors. Adapt processes per country-specific requirements.
  • Manage contract/budget amendments during the trial.
  • Update appropriate tracking systems to facilitate site payments.
  • Regularly attend internal and client project team meetings, as necessary
  • Collaborate with internal teams as needed (i.e., Project Management, Regulatory Affairs, Legal Affairs, Finance, CTMS team, etc.)
  • Strategize to ensure deliverables for fully executed contracts are made on time, according to study timelines.
  • Review and provide support to Regulatory Affairs on informed consent form (master template) to ensure subject compensation text is aligned with approved study budget.
  • Depending on location and language of study sites, facilitate site negotiations and communications using an intermediary party (i.e., contractor, sub-CRO or CRA)
  • Provide oversight to contractors and Sub-CROs, as well as Innovaderm SBCS across multiple countries on contracting activities, as required.
  • Act as functional lead for the contract management piece in global studies as required, acting as main POC of the sponsor regarding contract management matters.
  • Make all efforts to ensure total study budget is respected and within scope, across all sites. Escalates to sponsor for out-of-scope budget requests, as needed.
  • For employees located in Europe, aid, to communicate with sites in local language, if possible
  • Maintain adequate training and compliance with internal processes and SOPs.
  • Participate in internal departmental projects initiated by the site selection and contracting group.
  • Participate in internal departmental projects initiated by other groups to provide insight on site budget and contracting activities as needed.
  • Act as subject matter expert on budget and contract negotiations guiding project teams as needed with mentoring activities to junior team members.
  • Support the Manager, Site Selection and Contracting to ensure knowledge of the goals, scope and requirements of the internal and external projects and to ensure high quality results are delivered.

Requirements

Education 

  • Bachelor's degree in a field relevant to clinical research or equivalent experience.

Experience 

  • Minimum of 7 years’ experience in clinical research in site budget/contract negotiation in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or CRO industry, including significant and relevant experience in site selection, study start-up activities and/or has worked closely with sites or worked in a site environment.
  • Minimum 2 years’ experience in a similar contract lead role in the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or CRO industry

Knowledge and skills

  • Excellent English written and spoken skills. Bilingual with Spanish, German or Polish languages. Being fluent in 2+ EU languages is an asset.
  • Strong ability to carry out different projects simultaneously, to organize their work effectively, and to work under pressure in accordance with deadlines.
  • Excellent knowledge of the Microsoft Office suite (i.e., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
  • Prior clinical research experience in EU countries, and knowledge of local regulations and processes is an asset
  • Experience of dermatological and rheumatological clinical research is an asset
  • Ability to work under pressure and with tight timelines is essential.
  • Quick learner, good adaptability and versatile
  • Ability to work in a team environment and establish good relationships with colleagues, sponsors, and sites.
  • Organized, able to juggle competing priorities, and work in a fast pace and evolving environment.
  • Flexibility, positive attitude, superior attention to detail, and critical thinking skills

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Permanent full-time position
  • Flexible schedule
  • Vacation
  • Home-based position
  • Ongoing learning and development

About Indero

Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. Our full-service approach – which includes everything from protocol design and patient recruitment to trial monitoring and biometrics – provides biotech and pharmaceutical sponsors with the rigorous scientific foundation and tailored expertise their studies need to reach the finish line efficiently and effectively. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. As such, Indero will provide accommodations throughout the recruitment and selection process to applicants with disabilities, upon request.

jobs.title: Registrar and Director of Academic Records
jobs.excerpt: Role OverviewThe Registrar & Director of Academic Records is the senior institutional leader accountable for the design, construction, and ongoing integrity of every registrar function at Meritus College, from the student information system and academic catalog to degree audit, conferral, transfer credit, FERPA administration, and accreditation-facing reporting.
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Registrar & Director of Academic Records is the senior institutional leader accountable for the design, construction, and ongoing integrity of every registrar function at Meritus College, from the student information system and academic catalog to degree audit, conferral, transfer credit, FERPA administration, and accreditation-facing reporting.

This is a founding role in the literal sense. There is no legacy SIS configuration to maintain, no catalog to reprint, no degree audit to run, no policy manual to inherit. There is a first cohort, an accreditation timeline, a competency-based academic model that does not map cleanly onto conventional registrar practice, and a blank page. The Registrar decides and then documents, defends, and operationalizes how academic progress at Meritus College is measured, recorded, awarded, and reported.

The role carries three horizons simultaneously: keeping the current cohort running cleanly, building infrastructure that will hold at ten times the enrollment, and producing the evidence base that will withstand accreditation and federal scrutiny. The Registrar supports the college leadership team, and is the institution’s definitive authority on the student record.

What makes this role unusual

  • Full functional ownership: All registrar functions. The person in this seat sets the standard rather than administering someone else’s.
  • Design authority, not just execution authority: The policies, definitions, calendars, and data structures do not exist yet. This role writes them and shepherds them through governance.
  • Challenging technical problems: Translating a competency-based, mastery-progression model into a credit-hour-defensible, auditable, federally reportable record is one of the more interesting unsolved problems in the field. This role owns it.
  • Permanence. The architecture built in the first eighteen months will govern this institution’s records for decades.

Core Responsibilities

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

1. Build and Lead the Office of the Registrar

  • Draft the institutional policy stack. Draft, socialize, and shepherd through governance the full body of registrar policy: registration and enrollment, grading, academic standing, satisfactory academic progress, engagement and attendance, leave and withdrawal, transfer credit and prior learning, degree conferral, records retention, and transcript issuance.
  • Establish the Academic Catalog as the institutional document of record. Own its content architecture, approval workflow, version control, publication cycle, and archive and ensure the catalog, the enrollment agreement, and the SIS configuration never diverge from one another.
  • Stand up registrar service infrastructure. Build intake and case management, published service-level standards, escalation paths, and student- and faculty-facing self-service documentation so that the function scales on process rather than on heroics.
  • Define the system of academic authority. Establish who may change a grade, waive or substitute a requirement, release a record, reverse a withdrawal, or certify a completion and the documentation and audit trail required behind each action.
  • Support Implementation of SIS. Lead requirements definition, configuration, academic structure setup, and lifecycle governance; with IT Lead, make and defend the build decisions.

2. Own the Institutional Data of Record

  • Establish the institutional data dictionary for student records. Define and implement what constitutes enrollment, active status, the unit of academic progress, completion, and good standing, so that no two teams report different numbers for the same thing.
  • Institute data integrity controls. Build validation rules, reconciliation cycles, exception reporting, census-date freezes, and period-close discipline; personally certify the accuracy of official data before it leaves the institution.
  • Establish records custody, retention, and continuity. Set retention and destruction schedules, disaster recovery provisions, and the permanent record custody and teach-out plan required by regulators and accreditors.

3. Registration, Academic Progress, and Conferral

  • Own the academic calendar. Set and publish registration, add/drop, census, withdrawal, grading, and conferral dates across all programs and terms, and align them with financial aid, coaching, instruction, marketing, and enrollment operations.
  • Support enrollment lifecycle end to end. Registration, add/drop, withdrawal, leave of absence, reinstatement, track or program change, enrollment verification, and the learner-facing communication attached to each.
  • Build and own the degree audit. Encode program requirements, operate progression checks, resolve exceptions and substitutions with documented rationale, and certify candidates for conferral.
  • Design credential issuance end to end. Diploma production, digital credentials, transcript design and legend, secure delivery, and third-party degree verification.
  • Support transfer credit and prior learning. With academic leads, set evaluation criteria and faculty consultation protocols, establish articulation from Merit America programs and industry-recognized certifications into Meritus College credit, define awarding limits and residency requirements, and administer posting and appeals.

5. Accreditation and Regulatory Reporting

  • Produce the registrar’s contribution to accreditation. Author the relevant self-study sections, assemble and maintain the evidence file, and serve as a named institutional respondent in site visits, interim reports, and substantive change filings.
  • Own registrar-side state authorization obligations. Enrollment tracking by state, professional licensure disclosure records, complaint documentation, and coordination with institutional compliance on reciprocity and reauthorization requirements.
  • Support institutional effectiveness reporting. Define cohorts, census methodology, and persistence, retention, and completion metrics such that internal dashboards and external filings reconcile to the same source of truth.
  • Build registrar literacy across the institution. Train faculty, coaches, admissions, and student services on records obligations, FERPA, deadlines, and grading practice translating regulatory complexity into instructions people can actually follow.

Skills and Competencies

We recognize that individuals from marginalized backgrounds, including women, people of color, and those with disabilities, are often less likely to apply when they don’t meet 100% of the job qualifications. Don’t let that be the reason you miss out on this opportunity. Your unique skills, experiences, and perspectives are valuable, and we encourage you to apply if you can demonstrate many of the skills and competencies below.

Must Haves

Experience

  • Eight or more years of progressively responsible experience in a registrar’s office, academic records, or academic operations function in higher education, including at least three years at the associate registrar level or above.
  • Demonstrated ownership of core registrar systems and processes having personally led at least one substantial build or rebuild, such as an SIS implementation or migration, a degree audit build, a catalog or curriculum-of-record system, or a transcript and credentialing redesign.
  • Policy authorship experience. A track record of writing academic policy and moving it through institutional governance.
  • Accreditation experience. Direct participation in self-study, evidence preparation, site visits, substantive change filings, or annual reporting.

Technical and regulatory expertise

  • Deep FERPA fluency, including practical judgment in ambiguous disclosure situations, not only policy recitation.
  • Student information system expertise: the ability to define requirements, drive configuration decisions, understand the underlying data model, troubleshoot at the structural level, and hold vendors accountable. Experience with systems serving small or emerging institutions is as relevant as experience with enterprise platforms.
  • Working knowledge of the federal and state regulatory environment affecting academic records, Title IV eligibility requirements and their records implications, state authorization and reciprocity obligations, and institutional reporting requirements including IPEDS and Clearinghouse reporting.
  • Data fluency. The ability to define metrics precisely, interrogate data for integrity issues, produce accurate reporting, and explain discrepancies with confidence.

Nice To Haves

  • Comfort using AI tools to accelerate policy drafting, documentation, and research, with judgment about where they help and where they don't.
  • Experience in emerging, start-up programming, colleges or universities.

Other Logistics

  • Location:Remote
  • Salary: $112,000

We take care of our employees by providing the following perks and benefits (please note that some of the benefits do not apply to temporary employees):

  • Medical, Dental and Vision insurance (100% Paid Employee Only Coverage)
  • Flexible Spending Account and Health Savings Account
  • Dependent care Flexible Spending Account

jobs.title: Bioinformatics Customer Success Specialist
jobs.excerpt: About DNAstack At DNAstack, our mission is to power precision medicine by building software that breaks down barriers to responsible biomedical data sharing, discovery, and analysis.
jobs.description:
About DNAstack

At DNAstack, our mission is to power precision medicine by building software that breaks down barriers to responsible biomedical data sharing, discovery, and analysis. We build cutting-edge software and industry standards to help researchers and clinicians analyze sequencing data and make faster, more accurate diagnoses. Our platform supports national and international networks tackling rare disease, cancer, infectious disease, and more.

We’re a nimble, cross-functional team of scientists, engineers, designers, and product thinkers working at the intersection of genomics, software, and cloud technologies. Our mission is ambitious, and so is our team.

The Role

The Bioinformatics Customer Success Specialist makes sure every customer gets accurate, timely, and dependable results from the DNAstack platform. You are the technical owner of the customer experience after go-live: the first responder when a run fails, the person who confirms a result is right before it ships, and the voice that brings customer pain points back to engineering and product.

This is a growth-oriented role for an M.S.-level bioinformatician who enjoys both the science and the people. You will start on the front line of our operations: resolving support tickets, monitoring production pipelines across AWS and GCP, running and validating sample batches, and preparing custom deliverables for partners. That work gives you an intimate view of our architecture and of what customers actually need.

As your expertise grows, you will move from fixing issues to preventing them. You will build quality checks and regression tests, benchmark new tools against reference standards, maintain pipeline dependencies, and help set the reliability standards that our clinical and research customers depend on.

What You’ll Do

1. Customer Support and Issue Resolution

  • Serve as the primary technical point of contact for customer support tickets, partner inquiries, and data delivery requests.
  • Triage, diagnose, and resolve failed secondary and tertiary pipeline runs, annotation and sorting bugs, and cloud permission issues within agreed response times.
  • Lead root-cause investigations into missing variants, control sample mismatches (e.g., commercial reference controls), and runtime bottlenecks, and communicate findings clearly to customers.
  • Turn recurring issues into knowledge-base articles, runbooks, and FAQs so customers and teammates can self-serve.

2. Platform Quality and Reliability

  • Monitor production workflows and dataset deployments across GCP and AWS, catching failures and performance drift before customers notice.
  • Define and run quality-control checks on pipeline inputs and outputs, including sample identity, coverage, and variant-level QC metrics.
  • Run regression and validation tests on new pipeline and platform releases using reference materials (e.g., GIAB) before they reach customers.
  • Estimate and track workflow compute costs across cloud platforms, giving internal teams and customers realistic cost ranges for workflows and versions and informing selection of preferred cloud when onboarding new customers.
  • Document incidents with clear root cause, impact, and prevention steps, and track fixes through to completion with engineering.
  • Maintain and upgrade pipeline dependencies (e.g., Samtools, GATK, AnnotSV within WDL) with full re-validation.

3. Customer Onboarding and Data Operations

  • Onboard new customers: validate target capture files (BED), metadata sheets, and sample identifiers before first execution.
  • Create and maintain onboarding guides, runbooks, and FAQs for new customers, and own their success from first login through processing their samples at scale.
  • Submit, track, and verify routine sample runs and re-analyses across customer accounts.
  • Re-index, reload, and verify dataset nodes across deployment environments after updates.

4. Custom Deliverables and Customer Value

  • Generate customized data subsets, including read-supporting BAM slices, collection-level VCFs, and targeted TSV extracts.
  • Format and QC structural variant (SV), short tandem repeat (STR), and methylation outputs for partner handoffs.
  • Partner with Business Development on demo datasets, proofs of concept, and compute cost estimates for prospective customers.

5. Voice of the Customer (Growth)

  • Bring structured customer feedback to product and engineering to shape the roadmap and reliability priorities.
  • Benchmark variant callers and pipeline parameters to inform recommendations to customers.
  • Partner with the Staff Bioinformatician on exploratory features (e.g., new SV merging strategies) and join our internal bioinformatics journal club.

What We’re Looking For

  • Master's degree in computational biology, bioinformatics, biostatistics, computer science, or equivalent experience.
  • 1–3 years of professional experience in an industry biotech, diagnostic, or clinical bioinformatics role, ideally customer- or partner-facing.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication; able to explain complex technical issues to non-computational stakeholders.
  • Structured, methodical approach to troubleshooting and root-cause analysis.
  • Hands-on experience running and debugging NGS and -omics data processing pipelines.
  • Working knowledge of common genomics file types (FASTQ, BAM/CRAM, VCF, BED) and analysis tools.
  • Proficiency in Python (preferred), R, or Java, and a solid grasp of shell scripting and the command line.
  • Strong attention to detail and a sense of ownership for data quality.
  • Background in biology or genetics with proven critical thinking and research skills.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with workflow languages (e.g., WDL, CWL, Nextflow, Snakemake) and containers (Docker, Singularity).
  • Experience with cloud computing (GCP, AWS, Azure) or HPC environments, including monitoring and logging tools.
  • Experience with automated testing or CI/CD for bioinformatics pipelines.
  • Familiarity with quality systems or regulated environments (e.g., CAP/CLIA, ISO 13485) and validation documentation.
  • Experience with ticketing or customer success tools (e.g., Jira Service Management, Zendesk, Intercom).
  • Long-read sequencing experience (e.g., PacBio HiFi), including SV, STR, and methylation analysis.
  • Strong statistical skills and experience building effective data visualizations.
  • Wet lab genomics experience (e.g., library preparation, protocol design).
  • Experience using modern AI tools (e.g. Claude Code)

Why This Role Is Exciting

  • Impact at scale: Your work will directly influence tools used by national and international genomics networks.
  • Build something new: Shape a core function of the company from a small, senior team into a scalable, sustainable group.
  • Cross-disciplinary collaboration: Work side by side with engineers, product managers, and scientists to turn bioinformatics into real-world solutions.
  • Mission-driven: Contribute to solving rare disease, cancer, and infectious disease challenges by enabling precision medicine.
  • Team culture: Enjoy a flexible, remote-friendly team culture along with a competitive salary, benefits, and employee stock option program.

Where You'll Work

This role offers the flexibility of remote work, with the option to work in person from our Toronto office. This arrangement supports your needs and promotes a healthy work–life balance.

Eligibility

To be considered for this position, you must be eligible to work in Canada.

Benefits

  • Remote friendly, with flexible hours and the opportunity to work on-site at our Toronto office
  • Comprehensive health benefits: medical, dental and vision coverage for you and your dependents
  • Three weeks vacation
  • Unlimited sick days
  • Maternity and parental leave top-up programs
  • One-time remote office set-up stipend
  • Career development and learning support
  • Opportunity to participate in DNAstack's Employee Stock Option Program
  • Opportunity to contribute to open science and global data-sharing efforts

The salary range for this role is $70,000 to $95,000. At DNAstack, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at DNAstack is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other DNAstack team members.

DNAstack is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. In accordance with the appropriate legislation in each jurisdiction in which we operate, we ensure that our team members are compensated within equal pay ranges for work of equal value, regardless of gender.

We regularly review our compensation practices to identify and address any pay equity gaps. Our approach considers skill, effort, responsibility, and working conditions to ensure that compensation decisions are objective, transparent, and free from bias.

Pay equity is an ongoing process, and we are committed to maintaining compliance with legislative requirements while fostering a workplace that values fairness, respect, and inclusion.

At DNAstack, we are committed to building and fostering an inclusive, accessible environment for everyone. If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding accessibility needs at any stage of the interview process, please contact and we will work with you to meet your needs.

These tools help in areas such as sorting applications and highlighting matches to the role. These tools help us move faster, but they definitely don't make decisions for us - every application is reviewed by a real human on our team.

jobs.title: Staff Software Developer (copy)
jobs.excerpt: BackerKit helps creators bring projects to life.  For over a decade, we’ve powered some of the world’s most successful crowdfunding campaigns.
jobs.description:
BackerKit helps creators bring projects to life. For over a decade, we’ve powered some of the world’s most successful crowdfunding campaigns. We’re always building the next generation of our platform, innovating, and driving the industry forward.

We’re a remote-first company of ~40 people with a diverse, close-knit team that prizes creativity, enthusiasm, and a willingness to learn. We move quickly, think deeply about our users, and care about building software that lasts.

We’re looking for a full-time, Staff-level engineer who is deeply motivated by user experience, interaction design, and frontend craftsmanship and excited to bring that to life within a Ruby on Rails monolith. Perhaps this is you!

The role

This is a hands-on fullstack, product engineering role reporting to our Director of Engineering, Product, and Design. You’ll lead mainly through the code you write, review, and ship, and most of your week should be devoted to the team’s queue. We are looking for a UX- and business-minded engineer to work directly in Rails views to simplify complex workflows, create intuitive user experiences, and help transform the crowdfunding landscape.

You’ll help shape frontend patterns across the product, and turn our powerful, interconnected systems into intuitive experiences that are fast, clear, and approachable.

This role is high-context, high-collaboration, and high-impact. You’ll evolve patterns, raise the quality bar through mentorship and code review, and influence how the entire Engineering, Product & Design team thinks about user experience. Everyone at BackerKit is customer-facing, and we expect everyone to get to know the creators and backers that we serve (plus, they are awesome, just like you!).

How we build

We iterate quickly, ship small experiments, and learn from customers. We use Claude Code, practice TDD, work in one-week iterations, and ship multiple times a day.

We were a full-time pairing shop for over a decade, and pairing is still central to how we work. Right now we’re also experimenting with solo and cross-functional trio work as we figure out what a great product team looks like when everyone is also working alongside AI. Today we pair with intent: for complex or ambiguous work, knowledge transfer, onboarding, and a teammate’s growth. That balance is still evolving and may shift back toward more pairing, so we want someone who’s curious about how the team works today before helping us decide what comes next.

We’re pragmatic. Speed matters, but it isn’t a goal on its own; we want a pace we can sustain while still doing quality work and shipping the most impactful features for our business. Crowdfunding has real urgency and some chaos, so built into our values is the ability to respond quickly when creators, backers, and colleagues need us.

Our process keeps evolving, and we want your voice in it. As one of our most senior folks, you’ll bring strong opinions and your experience to those conversations. We’re highly collaborative, but we aren’t purely consensus-driven.

BackerKit is a Ruby on Rails “majestic monolith” deployed on Heroku. The codebase has been around since 2012. Despite that, it is relatively well-factored and well-tested. We’ve been tending this garden for over a decade!

We value simplicity, maintainability, communication, and shared ownership. We’re a remote-first team, and this role works the team’s shared hours, 9-5 Pacific. We work closely with teammates across the company and with the creators and backers we serve, so being reachable and ready to respond to what the day brings during those hours matters.

What you’ll do

  • Build alongside engineers, PMs, and designers in pairs, trios and solo, working on the most impactful features as we innovate the crowdfunding landscape

  • Lead frontend architecture, evolving patterns incrementally from real, repeated cases

  • Co-own features end to end, translating product and design intent into elegant, maintainable UI and following up on usage after launch

  • Simplify complex workflows and improve usability, responsiveness, and performance

  • Mentor engineers and set the bar for code quality through review, holding AI-generated code to a high standard

  • Report to our Director and join their engineering leadership group, alongside our other Staff Engineer and our CEO (a founding engineer who still codes daily), to advise on priorities and shape technical direction.

  • Carry your share of team rotations, including on-call, PR review, and meeting host, and take actual breaks and vacations, with no off-hours or weekend work required beyond your on-call shifts

What we’re looking for

Technical, craft, and process

  • Deep experience building high-quality user interfaces, and recent hands-on coding

  • Strong fundamentals in HTML, CSS, JS, and browser behavior

  • Comfort working directly in Rails views, helpers, and partials

  • Experience with or strong interest in Hotwire / Turbo / Stimulus

  • Preference for simple, maintainable systems over unnecessary abstraction

  • Values pairing, and genuine interest in exploring what that looks like in this new AI-enabled world (bonus if you’ve worked in a 100% pairing environment)

Product & UX thinking

  • Strong product and interaction design instincts

  • Experience simplifying complex workflows

  • Ability to work effectively with ambiguity

Staff-level impact

  • Experience shaping engineering patterns and conventions

  • Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills

  • Act as a go-to partner for complex or ambiguous frontend and UX challenges

  • Ability to zoom out to systems (architecture and business-level) thinking while remaining comfortable bushwhacking in the weeds

  • Comfort making your case on priorities, then committing to the decision once it’s made.

Most successful candidates for this role have 10+ years of software development experience working on multiple complex software projects over time and 5+ years as a staff engineer, though we do not have a strict years-of-experience requirement.

This role is a great fit if you

  • Have deep knowledge of Ruby, Rails, and JavaScript

  • Care deeply about how software feels to use

  • Enjoy working across product, design, and backend concerns

  • Prefer cohesive Rails applications over fragmented frontend stacks or SPAs

  • Treat constraints as a creative tool

  • Care about creators getting to make a living doing what they love

This role is likely not a fit if you

  • Prefer working in React, Vue, or SPA-heavy environments

  • Prefer fully decoupled frontend/backend architectures

  • Prefer long periods of solo or heads-down work

  • Prefer to set your own priorities rather than work from a shared team queue

  • Are looking for a part-time or contract role

Compensation & benefits

  • Full-time, salaried, remote-first position on a distributed team

  • Competitive salary and stock option plan

  • Medical, dental, vision, and 401k benefits (with employer match!)

  • Stipends for supporting creators of your choosing

  • Annual Learning and Development stipend to support your professional growth

  • Family-friendly and focused on maintaining a healthy work/life balance
  • Awesome work environment at a company with a huge opportunity

Research shows that while men apply for jobs when they meet ~60% of the criteria, women and other underrepresented groups tend to only apply when they check every box. If this role excites you – even if you don’t meet every requirement – we’d love to hear from you.

change detection, advanced analytics, and mission applications for governments and industries worldwide.

defining and driving EarthDaily's product strategy for defense and intelligence markets. The Director will
identify high-value mission problems and translate them into differentiated, scalable products that combine
EarthDaily's Earth observation data, analytics, AI/ML, contextual data, and workflow capabilities. This role is
highly outward-facing and will spend substantial time with government users, commercial customers,
acquisition stakeholders, Sales & Business Development, and industry partners to understand the market and
translate those insights into clear product priorities and requirements.

The role is part of EarthDaily's Analytics Product organization and works in close partnership with EarthDaily
Federal, Analytics line of business, and Engineering to develop defense and intelligence products for U.S.
Government and international defense agencies and customers. The Director owns the product problem,
customer outcome, product strategy, roadmap, requirements, prioritization, packaging, and commercial
product case. EarthDaily Federal and EarthDaily Analytics market teams along with Sales lead customer
relationships, capture, opportunity strategy, contracting, and revenue execution, while Engineering owns
technical design, delivery planning, sprint management, and implementation. The Director is expected to

revenue, stay close to customers and technical teams, and maintain a high level of responsiveness and

accountability.

What You'll Own

EarthDaily | Director, Product Management - Defense & Intelligence | 2

    • Pricing and packaging: Develop and evolve pricing, packaging, licensing, and value propositions for defense

    • Customer validation: Establish disciplined feedback and validation loops with government end users and

    • Cross-functional product leadership: Establish a working operating rhythm with Engineering in which
    Product provides customer context, clear priorities, requirements, and desired outcomes while technical
    teams own architecture, delivery planning, sprint execution, and implementation. Work closely with

    • Competitive and market intelligence: Track relevant commercial EO, GEOINT, analytics, AI/ML, workflow,

    • Executive product leadership: Communicate product strategy, customer evidence, investment choices,

Leadership Expectations

EarthDaily | Director, Product Management - Defense & Intelligence | 3

escalations.

What You Bring

jobs.title: Client Service Associate (Japanese speaker, WFH)
jobs.excerpt: OverviewYou are a matchmaker and project manager.
jobs.description:
Overview

You are a matchmaker and project manager. We have four products (Interpretation, Translation, Moderation and Transcripts). Customer service and client satisfaction are what motivate you to succeed.

You begin your tenure at Cadence assisting simple projects, and as you develop further, you will:

- Own more complex projects

- Own more client relationships

- Run teams

- Scale up workflows

About Us

Cadence () is a language services firm servicing the due diligence industry. We started in Beijing in 2014 and the types of clients we serve are expert networks, investment firms, consulting firms and market research firms. We are a remote-first company whose staff is located across multiple countries. Each individual is functionally aligned to one of three time zones (APAC, EMEA, Americas). We strive to promote internally whenever possible, so this is a limited opportunity to join a company that values ambitious and efficient professionals keen to develop their career.

Daily Responsibilities

You will manage multiple projects per day.

Projects can begin and end on the same day (”I need an interpreter for a call at 8pm tonight”).

Or they can span several weeks (”I am hosting three focus groups in three Japanese cities and need moderators to facilitate the focus groups and translate the output into English”).

Here’s how you will interact with a project:

Scoping

  • You will speak with clients via email, phone, or any other platforms (Whatsapp, WeChat etc.) about their needs
  • You will work with colleagues to ensure the client’s expectations for quality, speed, and cost are met
  • You will identify colleagues to assist based on the relevant time zones or regions for the project

Matchmaking

  • Your top responsibility is to identify the best linguist in our community for the client’s objective
  • You will need to present that linguists’ experience in a relevant way for the project
  • ... or you will need to recruit a new one if there isn’t an ideal match
  • You will need to constantly evaluate profitability and client satisfaction

Executing

  • You will need to sync up expectations between client(s) and linguist(s)
  • You may need to chaperone calls to ensure they begin successfully
  • You will need to speak with clients after projects to make sure they are satisfied

Key Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree
  • Native-level Japanese and professional-level English; other languages are a plus
  • Experience with Salesforce or similar CRM systems
  • Outgoing personality with ability to speak to professionals (junior or senior)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication and client service skills
  • Strong organizational and multitasking abilities
  • Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced environment
  • Ability to work effectively in both independent and team environments
  • Goal-oriented, driven, and highly motivated to succeed & take on challenges
  • Entry-level to intermediate-level candidates are welcome to apply: any relevant work experience is a plus

Working Hours & Location

  • You will follow your local business hours and holidays
  • This is a fully-remote role where you can work from home (WFH)

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary based on experience and location
  • Healthcare insurance and other health benefits
  • Annual allowance for professional development expenses

Work Authorization

  • This is a contractor status role.
  • We hire globally, and all team members for this position will be engaged as independent contractors.

Interview Process

1 - submit your CV in English.

2 - watch your email for instructions on how to submit a video selfie.

3 - have a screening call with our HR team (focus is the role's scope and working arrangement. A short case study is included.)

4 - meet potential co-workers (focus is to discuss your prior work and education experiences)

5 - final-round interview with our COO (focus is on your career fit)

Don’t meet every single requirement? Cadence values diversity and inclusion. Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every single qualification. We want a happy and engaged team, so if you like what you're reading but are worried you don't "check all the boxes", please apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

jobs.excerpt: About the OpportunityReporting to the Director of Enterprise Systems (and supported by the CTO in the Director's absence), the Enterprise Systems Manager is a hands-on, delivery-focused role at the centre of Prescient's enterprise technology function.
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

Reporting to the Director of Enterprise Systems (and supported by the CTO in the Director's absence), the Enterprise Systems Manager is a hands-on, delivery-focused role at the centre of Prescient's enterprise technology function.

Prescient's systems landscape is in a period of real and exciting change. We have recently implemented a new PSA platform, are actively developing our Salesforce capabilities, and are building the integrations and data foundations that will underpin how we operate as a business for years to come. The Enterprise Systems Manager will play a central role in shaping and delivering that agenda.

This is a role for someone who gets things done and thinks about what should be done next. You will own the day-to-day administration and health of our core systems, including Salesforce, CMap, BambooHR, Sage Intacct and Concur, while actively driving improvements, identifying where AI and automation can reduce friction, managing change and training, and helping the business get more from its technology investment.

As the Director's focus evolves towards product strategy and roadmap ownership, the Manager will take on increasing operational accountability, making this an excellent opportunity for someone with ambition, initiative and a genuine interest in how systems and processes can make a business better.

We would welcome someone based near our London or Manchester office but we don't want to limit access to top talent so we are open to remote working for the right person.

Responsibilities

System Administration and Day-to-Day Operations

  • Administer and maintain Prescient's core enterprise platforms on a day-to-day basis, including Salesforce, CMap (PSA), BambooHR, Sage Intacct, Concur and Boomi integration flows.
  • Manage user access, permissions, configuration changes and system health across in-scope platforms, ensuring stable and well-controlled operation.
  • Maintain accurate, up-to-date documentation of system configuration, integrations, business rules and standard operating procedures.
  • Act as first point of escalation for system queries and issues from across the business, triaging and resolving or routing to the appropriate vendor or specialist.

Programme and Project Coordination

  • Coordinate active workstreams across the enterprise systems programme, maintaining task lists, tracking progress and flagging risks or blockers to the Director.
  • Manage the programme plan and action log, ensuring owners are held to account and milestones are tracked accurately.
  • Prepare status updates, programme materials and briefing notes for steering committees and senior stakeholders.
  • Support the planning and execution of system implementations, configuration changes and releases, from requirements through to testing, training and go-live.
  • Coordinate UAT activity: building test scenarios, preparing test environments and data, facilitating sessions and logging and chasing the resolution of defects.

Data Management and Quality

  • Build and maintain standard reports, dashboards and data extracts to support operational and management needs.
  • Investigate data and process issues, identifying root causes and implementing sustainable fixes.

Continuous Improvement and Efficiency

  • Build and manage a live backlog of system and process improvement opportunities, working with stakeholders across the business to identify where technology can do more.
  • Lead the delivery of improvement initiatives end-to-end, from problem definition and solution design through to build, testing and embedding.
  • Challenge existing processes where they create friction, duplication or manual effort, and design better alternatives.
  • Identify and eliminate sources of manual effort and rework across system-supported processes, designing configurations that scale without constant intervention.
  • Ensure every system change lands properly: not just deployed, but adopted, understood and used correctly by the people it affects.

Change Management and Training

  • Own the change management approach for system changes and improvements, ensuring impacted teams understand what is changing, why, and what it means for them.
  • Design and deliver training for new and changed functionality, building materials that are clear, practical and tailored to the audience.
  • Develop and maintain a library of user guides, process documentation and quick reference materials, keeping them current as systems evolve.
  • Build a network of system champions across the business who support adoption and provide first-line guidance to their teams.

AI and Automation

  • Actively explore how AI and automation tools can be applied within Prescient's systems landscape to reduce manual effort, improve data quality and accelerate delivery.
  • Pilot and evaluate new capabilities within existing platforms, including AI features being released by vendors such as Salesforce, CMap and BambooHR.
  • Bring forward practical, well-scoped proposals for how AI and automation can solve real business problems, rather than technology for its own sake.
  • Stay current with developments in enterprise systems and AI tooling, bringing relevant insights back to the team.

Stakeholder, Business and Vendor Engagement

  • Act as the primary day-to-day point of contact for system queries, requests and improvement ideas from across the business, ensuring stakeholders feel heard and informed.
  • Organise and facilitate regular system champions meetings, bringing together key users from across practices to share updates, gather feedback and discuss improvement priorities.
  • Translate business requirements into clear, well-scoped functional specifications and configuration designs for review by the Director.
  • Maintain a clear, transparent prioritisation backlog, managing expectations honestly and ensuring the business understands what is being worked on, what is planned and what is not in scope. Challenge appropriately.
  • Push back confidently and constructively when requests cannot be delivered within available capacity, are not the right solution, or would create technical debt, offering alternatives where possible. Escalating where appropriate.
  • Communicate clearly about timelines, dependencies and trade-offs, avoiding over-commitment and building credibility through realistic planning and delivery.
  • Manage day-to-day operations with software vendors and implementation partners, raising and tracking support cases and ensuring issues are resolved within agreed service levels.
  • Provide input into vendor reviews, licence management and contract renewals.

Cover for the Director of Enterprise Systems

  • Hold operational responsibility for the enterprise systems function during periods when the Director is unavailable, with escalation support from the CTO.
  • Maintain sufficient working knowledge of the full systems landscape, active programmes and open issues to represent the function confidently to internal stakeholders.
  • Make day-to-day operational decisions within agreed parameters, escalating to the CTO only where strategic direction is required.

About You

Essential

  • Minimum 5 years experience in a systems administration, business systems, or operations coordination role. You will be comfortable owning platforms and managing data day to day.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one major enterprise platform (e.g. Salesforce, a PSA tool such as CMap or Kantata, an HRIS such as BambooHR or Workday, or a finance system such as Sage Intacct or NetSuite).
  • Strong organisational skills and a proven ability to manage multiple priorities, track tasks across complex workstreams and deliver to deadlines.
  • A proactive, action-oriented approach: you identify what needs doing and do it, rather than waiting to be told.
  • Clear, confident communication skills, with the ability to engage business stakeholders and explain system or process topics in plain language.
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced, changing environment where priorities can shift and pragmatic decisions are needed.
  • High attention to detail, particularly when managing data, configurations or programme documentation.

Desirable

  • Experience supporting a system implementation, migration or integration project in a coordination or analyst role.
  • Familiarity with integration platforms or middleware (e.g. Boomi, MuleSoft, Workato) at a working level.
  • Experience with reporting and dashboard tools (e.g. Power BI, Salesforce reports).
  • Knowledge of the pharmaceutical services, life sciences or professional services industry.
  • Relevant qualifications or platform certifications (e.g. Salesforce Administrator, ITIL Foundation) are a plus but not required.

What We Offer

  • A competitive salary and benefits package.
  • A high-growth, entrepreneurial environment with genuine responsibility from day one. This is not a support role.
  • Rapid exposure to a broad enterprise technology landscape across CRM, PSA, finance, HR and integration platforms.
  • A clear development path: as the Director's focus evolves, the Manager will take on increasing operational leadership of the function.
  • A collaborative team and direct line of sight to senior leadership, including the CTO and Director of Enterprise Systems.

About Prescient Healthcare Group

Prescient Healthcare Group is a specialist pharmaceutical consulting firm, partnering with biopharmaceutical clients to turn science into commercial value. Our practices span Competitive Strategy, Medical, Real World Evidence, VP&A and Commercial, supporting some of the world's leading life sciences organisations.

We are currently in an exciting period of growth and transformation, with a major programme under way to replace and consolidate our core enterprise systems. The Enterprise Systems Manager will play a hands-on role in delivering that programme and in operating the systems that underpin how we work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and fully comply with applicable employment legislation across all geographies in which we operate.

jobs.excerpt: iFIT’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience.
jobs.description:
iFIT’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience. We develop proprietary software that learns and adjusts to the habits of each person as it delivers immersive content that guides them on their own individual fitness journey.

We're hiring a Director, Digital Analytics & Experimentation to own the numbers behind our direct-to-consumer business on nordictrack.com. This is a global role spanning analytics, reporting, forecasting and experimentation, with subscription growth and the customer journey at the center. Leaders across the company make spending, pricing and merchandising decisions on your numbers.

Why join iFIT and NordicTrack

Connected fitness is a growing category at the center of health and wellness, and iFIT and NordicTrack are right in it. We sell more than equipment: the iFIT membership keeps customers training, so every conversion, test and forecast is a lifetime-value decision, not a one-time sale.

As our Director, you'll be the person leadership turns to for what's working, what's next and what it's worth, with a direct line to the executives making the calls. You'll shape the nordictrack.com experience, grow customer lifetime value, and help us move to a new AI-driven personalization platform.

What you'll do

The role splits roughly evenly across three areas, and you own the integrity of all three.

Analytics and data

  • Pull and validate data from web analytics, order, media and finance sources, and keep documented KPI definitions as one source of truth.
  • Diagnose performance changes by traffic source, product and funnel step, and make recommendations supported by quantified evidence.
  • Track, analyze and report on our subscription economics, including customer lifetime value (LTV) and the annual iFIT subscription attach rate, and show what moves them.
  • Map the customer journey from first visit through purchase and subscription, find what drives conversion and what blocks it, and tell us where to optimize first.

Reporting and forecasting

  • Own the daily, weekly and monthly performance reporting and the dashboards behind it, including LTV and subscription attach.
  • Prepare executive-ready summaries of results versus plan and prior year, with the drivers behind each variance.
  • Build and maintain the full P&L forecast for the DTC business, from traffic, conversion and subscription attach through revenue, margin and marketing spend, including media mix.

jobs.title: Ehrenamt · 5–8 Std./Woche: Legal Counsel / Compliance (m/w/d)
jobs.excerpt: Du bist Jurist:in oder kennst dich mit Vereinsrecht, Compliance und Governance aus – und möchtest dein Wissen für das Gemeinwohl einsetzen?
jobs.description:
Du bist Jurist:in oder kennst dich mit Vereinsrecht, Compliance und Governance aus – und möchtest dein Wissen für das Gemeinwohl einsetzen? Vielleicht suchst du neben deinem Beruf ein Pro-bono-Engagement mit Sinn, oder du bist im (Vor-)Ruhestand und willst deine Erfahrung weitergeben. Bei uns sorgst du dafür, dass eine wachsende Organisation rechtlich sauber aufgestellt ist – von der Satzung über die Geschäftsordnung bis zur Compliance.

Gleich vorweg: Das ist ein Ehrenamt

Die Aufgabe ist unbezahlt und begründet kein Beschäftigungsverhältnis. Sie lässt sich gut neben einem Hauptberuf ausüben.

Wer wir sind

Der Deutsche Hilfsbund e.V. (DEHIB) bündelt humanitäre, soziale und wirtschaftliche Initiativen und bringt Hilfsorganisationen mit Menschen aus Wirtschaft, Politik und Wissenschaft zusammen. Gemeinsam schaffen wir nachhaltige Strukturen für Chancengleichheit und soziale Unterstützung. Damit das auf einem festen Fundament steht, brauchen wir klare Regeln, saubere Verträge – und dich.

Deine Aufgaben

Recht, Satzung & Gremien

  • Satzung, Geschäftsordnung und weitere Ordnungen gemeinsam mit uns im Blick behalten, pflegen und weiterentwickeln
  • Bundesvorstand und Geschäftsführung bei rechtlichen und organisatorischen Fragen beraten
  • Verträge begleiten: Kooperations- und Projektvereinbarungen, Mandate, interne Richtlinien
  • Gremiensitzungen und Vorstandsbeschlüsse rechtlich vor- und nachbereiten
  • Disziplinarische Fragen und interne Verfahren nach unseren Ordnungen begleiten

Compliance, Datenschutz & Risiko

  • Compliance-Vorgaben verwalten und mit Vorstand und Geschäftsführung sicherstellen, dass sie eingehalten werden
  • Datenschutzfragen klären – zusammen mit unserem externen Datenschutzbeauftragten
  • Rechtliche Risiken früh erkennen, pragmatische Lösungen finden und unser Risiko- und Eskalationsmanagement mit aufbauen
  • Nachvollziehbare Abläufe für Dokumentation und Freigaben schaffen

Was du mitbringst

  • Juristisches Studium, eine vergleichbare Qualifikation oder fundierte Praxiserfahrung in Recht, Compliance oder Governance
  • Erfahrung im Vereins- oder Gesellschaftsrecht, im Datenschutz oder mit Non-Profit-Organisationen ist ein Plus
  • Du erklärst komplexe Sachverhalte verständlich und pragmatisch – auch gegenüber Vorstand und externen Partnern
  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, verantwortungsbewusst und mit Fingerspitzengefühl für sensible Themen
  • Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse (C1/C2) und sicherer Umgang mit Microsoft 365; Erfahrung mit Teams, OneDrive oder SharePoint ist von Vorteil
  • Verlässlichkeit: Du bist bereit uns regelmäßig mit 5–8 Stunden pro Woche zu unterstützen

Was wir dir bieten

Sinn & Gemeinnutz

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Hilfe auf einem rechtlich sicheren Fundament steht – und damit dort ankommt, wo sie gebraucht wird.
  • Du arbeitest mit Menschen, die Verantwortung übernehmen und gesellschaftlich etwas bewegen wollen.

Exklusives Netzwerk

  • Zugang zu einem wachsenden Netzwerk aus Wirtschaft, Politik, Wissenschaft und Non-Profit-Organisationen
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit Bundesvorstand, Geschäftsführung und zentralen Entscheidungsträger:innen
  • Austausch mit Unternehmer:innen, Führungskräften und Expert:innen ganz unterschiedlicher Fachrichtungen

Gestaltung & Verantwortung

  • Du gestaltest Governance, Compliance und Strukturen eines modernen Sozialverbands von Anfang an mit
  • Viel Eigenverantwortung, großer Gestaltungsspielraum und hohe Sichtbarkeit

Entwicklung & Referenz

  • Praxis in Vereinsrecht, Governance und Organisationsentwicklung einer bundesweit tätigen Organisation
  • Eine starke Referenz für deinen Lebenslauf und auf Wunsch ein qualifiziertes Ehrenamtszeugnis

So arbeiten wir zusammen

  • Flexible Zeiteinteilung, gut vereinbar mit deinem Hauptberuf – digital über Microsoft 365
  • Klare Absprachen: Aufgaben, Zeitumfang und feste Termine halten wir in einer kurzen Ehrenamtsvereinbarung fest
  • Gute Einarbeitung, eine feste Ansprechperson und eine Kennenlernphase von zwei bis drei Monaten

So meldest du dich – ganz unkompliziert

Du möchtest den DEHIB rechtlich und strukturell mit aufbauen? Dann schreib uns in drei, vier Sätzen, was du mitbringst und warum dich dieses Ehrenamt reizt. Danach lernen wir uns virtuell für 30 Minuten kennen und schauen gemeinsam, ob es passt.

jobs.description:
Description

MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare platform setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.

We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi's technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.

As Staff Product Designer, you will own the end-to-end design of MEDvidi's AI Track, the core line of AI-powered clinical tools where providers interact with model outputs in a regulated healthcare environment. Your design decisions directly shape how clinicians review, accept, and correct AI-generated notes, treatment plans, and recommendations, impacting both provider efficiency and patient outcomes.

You will work closely with product managers and engineers, reporting to the Director of Product. This is a senior IC role with no direct reports: you drive product design from problem definition through delivery, gather requirements independently, and bring solutions to release. Your scope includes provider-facing tools (Chart Review, AI Scribe, AI Receptionist), patient portal, and internal operational systems, all web-based.

Why this role

  • Zero-to-one in AI-first environment. You will shape new interaction patterns for agentic AI features: Chart Review, AI Scribe, AI Receptionist, where design quality directly affects clinical decisions.
  • Prototype in real code, not Figma mockups. Prototyping happens in Claude Code and Cursor on the actual codebase with production components. Your prototypes go straight to engineering without redrawing.
  • Co-own a design system built for humans and AI agents. You will evolve reusable components, tokens, and documentation that are readable by both your teammates and code-generation agents, a rare opportunity to define what design systems look like in an AI-native workflow.

Responsibilities

  • Own product design in your areas of the AI Track end-to-end: from defining the problem with the product manager, through user analysis, to working with engineers on the solution and accepting the build.
  • Design and iterate on human-AI interaction patterns: interfaces where providers verify, accept, edit, or reject model output and bring those patterns to a state where other teams can reuse them.
  • Ensure quality of design decisions: validate solutions with users when needed, perform design acceptance with engineering, analyze post-release results, and feed learnings back into the product.
  • Contribute to the design system within product initiatives: turn your solutions into reusable components in Storybook with tokens, naming, and documentation that are usable by both designers and AI code-generation agents.
  • Gather requirements independently: go to providers, medical operations, and product managers, identify problems, and bring back a proposal. There is no standing PM brief in AI Track, you shape the brief.
  • Accelerate design delivery using AI tools: build functional prototypes in Claude Code or Cursor on the real codebase with production components; prototypes go to engineering without redrawing.

This role is not for you if

  • You need a detailed brief before starting work. Requirements here are gathered by you, not handed to you, there is no PM or BA writing specs for AI Track.
  • You prefer managing people over hands-on design. This is an IC role with no direct reports; the impact comes from the quality of your own design decisions.
  • You design exclusively in Figma and hand off static specs. Prototyping at MEDvidi happens in code on the real codebase using AI agents, comfort with a code editor is a daily requirement, not a nice-to-have.

Requirements

  • 6+ years in product design, with a focus on complex work interfaces: EHR, admin panels, CRM, operational tools, or other systems where specialists perform their core work.
  • Demonstrable experience designing human-AI interaction: interfaces where users verify, accept, edit, or reject model output. Building a 0-to-1 agentic product is ideal; experience with review-and-approval interfaces for automated decisions also qualifies.
  • Hands-on prototyping in code using AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent) on an existing component library or codebase, not just design tools.
  • Track record of contributing to a design system within product work: shipping reusable components, tokens, and documentation as part of feature delivery, not as a standalone project.
  • Proven ability to gather requirements independently, finding problems, talking to users and stakeholders, and driving a solution to release without waiting for a mandated brief.
  • Advanced English (B2+) and fluent Russian.
  • Availability to work within CET-compatible hours.

Would be a plus

  • Experience in healthcare or telemedicine products: understanding of HIPAA, clinical compliance constraints, and the provider's role in decision-making.
  • Experience leading a design team's transition to AI tools: setting up shared agent workflows, running workshops, driving adoption across peers.
  • Hands-on user research with specialist users: usability testing and interviews with doctors, nurses, or clinical operators (not only end consumers).

What we offer

  • High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space.
  • Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package.
  • Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model.
  • Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation.
  • Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply.
  • Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days.
  • Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events.

Ready to make an impact? Send us your profile, let's build something meaningful together.

jobs.excerpt: Job Description: Elastic Stack Engineer(Search & Observability)Role OverviewAs an Elastic / Observability & Security Platform Engineer, you will lead the design, implementation, monitoring and continuous improvement of our Elastic-based observability and security stack.
jobs.description:
Job Description: Elastic Stack Engineer

(Search & Observability)

Role Overview

As an Elastic / Observability & Security Platform Engineer, you will lead the design,

implementation, monitoring and continuous improvement of our Elastic-based observability and security stack. You will take ownership of detection rules, watchers, ML-models, health monitoring of data streams, alerting frameworks, and tracking of data pipeline latency/integration times. You will work closely with data engineers, security operations, platform engineering, and business-units to ensure robust real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, alerting, and data integration observability.

Key Responsibilities

•

Architect, deploy, configure and optimise the Elastic Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana,

Beats, Logstash, Elastic Machine Learning, Elastic Watcher/Alerting).

•

Develop and maintain JSON-based configuration files, logic and pipelines for

detection rules, watchers and alerting states.

•

Design, build and operationalise machine-learning jobs within Elastic ML (e.g.,

anomaly detection, forecasting, classification) for observability/security use-cases.

•

Monitor, maintain and improve the health and performance of data-streams (logs,

metrics, events, traces) ingesting into the Elastic cluster: ensure data freshness,

minimal latency, correct mapping, index lifecycle management (ILM), shard

management, and cluster health.

•

Implement and maintain alerting/notification frameworks: watchers/triggers, custom

alert-logic via JSON, integration with downstream systems (Slack, Teams,

PagerDuty, email, webhook).

•

Track and report on the integration time between upstream data sources and the

Elastic ingestion pipeline (i.e., latency from source → pipeline → index →

availability), diagnose and mitigate delays or bottlenecks.

•

Develop dashboards, visualisations and reports in Kibana to communicate KPIs,

SLAs (data-ingestion, alert-response, model accuracy), and to drive continuous

improvement.

•

Collaborate with data engineering, DevOps, security operations (SecOps), SRE and

business stakeholders to define requirements and deliver effective

observability/security solutions.

•

Establish best‐practices, standards and documentation for JSON rule-configs,

watchers, ML-jobs, dashboarding and monitoring.

•

Participate in incident-response processes: support triage, root-cause analysis and feed

learnings back into detection rules/ML jobs/monitoring.

•

Stay up-to-date and contribute to improving the Elastic ecosystem in our

environment: new features, upgrades, tuning, cost-optimisation, benchmark/scale

testing.

Required Skills & Experience

•

Strong hands-on experience with the Elastic Stack (Elasticsearch, Kibana, Beats,

Logstash or equivalent ingestion pipelines) – you should be comfortable deploying,

configuring and operating production Elastic clusters.

•

Proficiency in writing and using JSON configurations and logic for detection rules,

watchers, alerting frameworks, and monitoring pipelines.

•

Experience building and operationalising Elastic Machine Learning jobs (anomaly

detection, forecasting, classifications) and interpreting model output for

observability/security use-cases.

•

In-depth experience monitoring and maintaining the health of high-volume data

streams: log/metric/event/tracing data, with attention to data latency, ingestion

batching, pipeline failures, index lifecycle, and cluster resource optimisation.

•

Experience designing end-to-end alerting workflows (trigger logic, thresholds, multi-

condition rules, escalation, notification integration).

•

Experience tracking and measuring integration times (data latency from source

ingestion to availability in index/dashboards) and implementing improvements to

reduce that latency.

•

Strong scripting or programming ability (e.g., Python, Bash, or similar) to automate

tasks, integrations or alert-logic.

•

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills: ability to diagnose

ingestion/pipeline/cluster issues, chain of events, root causes, and propose

mitigations.

•

Excellent communication skills: able to articulate detection logic, ML-model results,

data‐latency issues and dashboards to technical and non‐technical stakeholders.

•

Good understanding of DevOps/SRE practices (CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code,

Monitoring, Logging, Alerting).

•

Ability to document clearly: JSON rule setups, watchers, dashboards, models,

runbooks.

•

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or equivalent

experience; or equivalent relevant industry experience.

Desirable / Bonus Skills

•

Experience with elastic security (formerly SIEM) use‐cases using Elastic.

•

Experience with other observability/tracing stacks (OpenTelemetry, Jaeger,

Prometheus, Grafana) and integrating them into Elastic.

•

Knowledge of cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP) and experience managing

Elastic clusters in cloud or hybrid deployments.

•

Experience with large scale index management, shard tuning, ILM policies, cluster

scaling, and cost optimisation.

•

Experience with advanced ML-techniques (unsupervised learning, time‐series

forecasting, advanced feature engineering) applied to observability/security.

•

Knowledge of security operations (SecOps) and detection use-cases: threat hunting,

anomaly detection, SOC workflows.

•

Familiarity with infrastructure instrumentation (logs, metrics, traces) and analysing

telemetry from microservices/distributed systems.

We're looking for a Marketing Design Team Lead who is equal parts creative leader, marketer, and AI geek, someone who knows how to achieve business goals through visuals that actually sell.

You will take a team of 3 AI-driven Creative Designers and scale it to 6. The team produces static ad creatives, photorealistic AI visuals for performance campaigns across paid media channels, and source assets for our video production pipeline.

Your job is to build the company's visual creative engine. Whatever the starting point- a brief, a hypothesis, a raw idea - it leaves the team as a creative that performs.

You'll work closely with Creative Producers, Marketers, Copywriters, Media Buyers, and the Video Editing team, and partner with our Generative AI Pipeline Engineer on tooling and workflows.

  • Track new AI models and tools; be the company's go-to expert on what's creatively possible with AI, staying hands-on in the tools;
  • Run regular R&D and build prompt and style libraries that keep quality consistent as the team grows;
  • Stay hands-on: jump into the tools (Figma, Adobe Suite, AI platforms) when needed to unblock the team, take on the most complex creatives, or test new approaches;
  • Partner with the Generative AI Pipeline Engineer to turn the team's creative needs into pipelines, presets, and automation;
  • Work tightly with Creative Producers, Marketers, Media Buyers, and Video Editors: align on strategy, negotiate deadlines, solve bottlenecks.

Requirements

Hands-on with modern AI image platforms (Figma Weave, Higgsfield, Magnific, Runway, or similar), using them for creating photorealistic visuals. Forecasting and Sales Reviews

  • Manage the weekly forecasting cycle, including submission deadlines, data checks, consolidated reporting, and meeting preparation

  • Track forecast performance and investigate variances with the relevant sales teams

Pipeline Management and CRM Discipline
