jobs.title: IC – Construction Estimator I
jobs.excerpt: Remote | Outside the United StatesBefore You ApplyIC means Independent Contractor.
jobs.description:
Remote | Outside the United States

Before You Apply

IC means Independent Contractor. This is an independent contractor service opportunity intended for professionals located in and providing services from outside the United States. It is not an employee position and does not include Company employee benefits.

Service providers are expected to provide their own computer, reliable internet connection, and two additional monitors (three screens total). High-Light Electric will provide access to the software, licenses, Company virtual desktop, systems, and platforms required to perform the contracted services.

Independent contractors control how they organize and perform their services, subject to agreed deliverables, bid deadlines, coordination requirements, confidentiality obligations, and the terms of the Independent Contractor Agreement.

About the Opportunity

High-Light Electric, Inc. is building an estimating structure that clearly separates quantity takeoff from full bid ownership.

Takeoff Specialists measure and organize quantities. Estimators take that work forward — reviewing the takeoff, verifying scope, pricing the work, managing bid communication, assembling the estimating package, and owning the bid from start to finish.

We are currently seeking professionals who can provide Estimator I-level services, owning standard construction bids from initial review through bid submission and post-award handoff.

Depending on a candidate's existing estimating experience and demonstrated readiness to own a complete bid, the path into an Estimator I scope may begin with a Takeoff Specialist II engagement to demonstrate advanced scope recognition, prime-bid takeoff capability, and readiness for full estimating responsibility.

Services & Deliverables

As an Estimator I, your contracted services will include:

  • Run standard construction bids from initial review through bid submission and post-award handoff.
  • Review and approve assigned takeoff packages, verifying quantities, plans, specifications, materials, installation requirements, scope completeness, coordination items, and bid risks.
  • Price and assemble complete estimating packages, including bid worksheets, vendor and subcontractor quotes, bidder questions, addenda, and subcontractor information.
  • Manage standard bid-related communication with vendors, subcontractors, owners, agencies, and other external project contacts through Company-authorized communication channels, escalating complex or nonstandard matters when appropriate.
  • Coordinate pre-bid and bid-closeout reviews and provide a clear estimating recommendation before submission.
  • After award, support contract execution, budget setup, required project documentation, and a clean handoff to the project team, and remain available for questions regarding the estimate and how the work was priced.
  • Coordinate with Takeoff Specialists on assigned bid packages, including deadlines, package review, corrections, and missing information needed to complete the estimate.

The Estimator I is accountable for the completeness and quality of the final estimating package, including work incorporated from supporting takeoff packages.

What We're Looking For

A strong Estimator I should already be able to independently manage a standard construction bid from start to finish, rather than only performing quantity takeoffs.

Strong candidates will demonstrate:

  • Practical construction estimating experience, including pricing and bid preparation.
  • Experience reading and interpreting construction plans and specifications in English.
  • Strong understanding of scope and the ability to identify missing, conflicting, or incomplete information.
  • Experience reviewing takeoffs, vendor/subcontractor quotes, addenda, and other bid documents.
  • Strong Excel proficiency required.
  • Experience with Bluebeam Revu strongly preferred.
  • Professional written and verbal English for estimating discussions and external bid-related communication.
  • Strong attention to detail while maintaining an understanding of the complete bid.
  • Clear, proactive communication when scope, pricing, quality, or bid deadlines may be affected.
  • Accountability for the accuracy and completeness of contracted deliverables.
  • Sound judgment when working with confidential pricing, plans, specifications, and competitive information.
  • Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with Estimating, Operations, and project teams.

Experience with U.S. construction, electrical infrastructure, civil scope, or public works is highly valuable.

How the Engagement Works

This is a deliverable-based independent contractor engagement, not a fixed-shift or timesheet-based position.

Contractors determine how they organize their work as long as agreed deliverables and bid deadlines are met.

Because construction bidding depends on vendor quotes, agenda, bidder questions, pre-bid coordination, and bid closeouts, some activities occur according to external schedules. California business hours are generally 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Pacific Time.

You are not expected to work a fixed 8–5 shift; however, you must be able to coordinate and remain reachable during the specific California-business-hour windows required for active bids.

All work-related communication and external bid communication must be conducted through Company-authorized systems and platforms so project information remains secure and properly documented.

Contractor Fees

Estimator I

Monthly Service Fee: $2,400 USD*

Productivity Bonuses: $533 USD per $1M on jobs won

*The monthly service fee is invoiced through the regular contractor payment cycle subject to a mutually agreed scope of work provided upon successful engagement.

Productivity Bonuses may be earned on jobs won and are paid at the end of the month following the month in which they are earned, provided there are no unresolved estimating errors or outstanding rework associated with the applicable bid.

Production compensation is variable and depends on successfully awarded work.

These amounts are independent contractor service fees, not salary or wages. Final payment terms and conditions will be documented in the Independent Contractor Agreement.

Estimator Scope & Growth Path

Estimator I is responsible for standard construction bids from start to finish.

Candidates with demonstrated experience owning complete bids may be considered directly for an Estimator I engagement. Depending on experience and technical assessment, however, we will gladly consider less experienced but highly motivated candidates who will be engaged in a hybrid agreement to work for a set period as a Takeoff Specialist - with a written plan and provisions to learn the Estimator role while earning and learning. Takeoff Specialist involves advanced takeoff work on prime bids, including identifying electrical and civil scope, subcontracted work, coordination items, and missing information within the bid documents. Consistently demonstrating the judgment, accuracy, and scope awareness required at this level can establish readiness for an Estimator I scope. Contractors who later demonstrate the ability to handle greater bid complexity, autonomy, accuracy, and judgment may become eligible for an Estimator II expanded scope as business needs develop.

Estimator II handles large, complex, or multi-discipline bids, manages owner and agency communication with greater autonomy, and helps develop the takeoff function.

Estimator II Monthly Service Fee: $2,750 USD*
Estimator II Productivity Bonuses: $667 USD per $1M on jobs won

Changes in scope are not automatic or tenure-based. Eligibility is based on demonstrated capability, results, technical readiness, and business need.

About Mendoza Companies

Mendoza Companies is a multi-entity ecosystem of construction, services, and investment businesses operating under The Mendoza Way. The ecosystem includes High-Light Electric, Inc. (HLE) — a California-based union electrical infrastructure contractor founded in 1996 delivering public works and complex electrical construction across California — along with Mendoza Trust and an international independent contractor workforce.

We partner with Caltrans, municipalities, transit authorities, and infrastructure programs throughout California, with active expansion into Nevada, Arizona, and additional U.S. markets.

Mendoza Companies is guided by Mission 2040: the Mendoza Companies will be a $1-billion-dollar company, connecting 1,000 families and communities through business.

What to Expect in the Selection Process

Our selection process may include an AI-assisted interview through an authorized interviewing platform, followed by a conversation with Talent Acquisition via Microsoft Teams and additional interviews with members of our Estimating team and Company leadership.

Candidates who receive an AI interview invitation as part of this process should know that it is an authorized step in Mendoza Companies' recruiting process.

Equal Opportunity in Contractor Engagement

We are committed to providing equal opportunity in the selection and engagement of qualified independent contractors and do not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. This opportunity is for an independent contractor relationship and does not constitute an offer of employment.

Salary: $2,400 USD monthly

jobs.excerpt: About MeridiaMeridia is an agtech company built around the first mile: the plots, farmers and aggregation points at the origin of every agriculture supply chain.
jobs.description:
About Meridia

Meridia is an agtech company built around the first mile: the plots, farmers and aggregation points at the origin of every agriculture supply chain. Our first mile intelligence combines what field teams see on the ground and what satellites see from above, in the context of local law, foreign regulation and international frameworks. It rests on over a decade of field experience, our data lake covering 20%+ of the world’s agricultural land, a network of origin experts across the global South and a stellar team of 70+ agriculture, data and tech experts.

Meridia Verify®, our verification solution, checks supply chain field data against regulatory and voluntary sustainability frameworks in minutes and guides teams from risk detection to resolution. One platform covers EUDR, Deforestation- and Conversion-Free (DCF) commitments and Scope 3 land-use emissions at plot level, and benchmarks a supply chain against sector baselines.

Meridia Illuminate®, our sourcing intelligence solution, leverages the same first-mile data foundation to support secure sourcing decisions and resilient supply chains for the operators who shape global food and agriculture trade.

See for more information on our work.

Introduction

This document outlines the scope and objectives for hiring a consultant to support Meridia's first-mile intelligence work: the data science that connects commodity supply chains to the production areas they source from. This includes production area assessment, supply shed modelling and traceability, drawing on a variety of data sources and combining geospatial, statistical and ML approaches.

Understanding where commodities come from, without needing every farm boundary, helps buyers make credible, evidence-based sourcing risk assessments, while keeping smallholders included in supply chains. It supports deforestation- and conversion-free (DCF), EUDR and Scope 3-related risk assessment.

Objectives

  • Develop accurate, high-quality models and datasets for production area assessment and sourcing area (supply shed) analysis across multiple commodities and origin countries.
  • Leverage Meridia's in-situ farm plot datasets to train and validate models.
  • Adapt existing machine learning models to local agricultural contexts to improve prediction accuracy.
  • Create scalable and reproducible methodologies that work across different geographies and commodities.

Deliverables

  1. Methodology and codebase
  2. Organised folder with all source files
  3. Full documentation including operating workflow, methodology, sources (including retrieval and licensing details)

Requirements

Must have

  • Advanced degree (MSc or PhD) in Remote Sensing, Geospatial Science, Computer Science, or related field.
  • 10+ years of practical experience in applying statistical and earth observation techniques to agricultural applications.
  • Proficiency in programming languages commonly used in geospatial analysis and machine learning (Python, R, Google Earth Engine).
  • Knowledge of agricultural systems and supply chains in tropical and subtropical regions.
  • Experience with modelling approaches relevant to supply chain analysis, such as optimisation, spatial allocation, entity matching or network analysis across heterogeneous datasets.
  • Strong geospatial data engineering skills: spatial databases (e.g. PostGIS), GDAL/geopandas or equivalent, and handling of large raster and vector datasets.
  • Experience building reproducible, version-controlled analytical pipelines (Git; containerisation such as Docker is a plus).
  • Proven ability to document methodologies rigorously, including data provenance, assumptions, limitations and licensing.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote setting, with strong communication skills and full professional proficiency in English.

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with agri-commodity sectors (e.g. palm oil, soy, rubber, cocoa, coffee) and their data landscape, including production statistics, mill or processor lists, and sourcing structures with producers and intermediaries.
  • Familiarity with (agricultural) supply chain transparency and traceability approaches, logistics, procurement and certification.
  • Working knowledge of relevant frameworks (EUDR, DCF/NDPE, certification schemes) and how production area and sourcing area information supports risk assessment under them.
  • Experience validating models against ground-truth or in-situ field data, and quantifying and communicating uncertainty.
  • Experience working with production statistics and yield data in data-scarce environments.
  • Track record of peer-reviewed publications or public technical documentation in a related domain.
  • Prior experience in Southeast Asia and/or Latin America.

Benefits

This is an independent consultancy assignment rather than an employment role. Here is what you can expect from working with us:

  • Initial 3-month engagement, with possible extension depending on progress and mutual fit
  • 2-3 days per week
  • Fully remote
  • Software subscriptions provided by Meridia where applicable
  • Monthly invoicing against agreed milestones and deliverables
  • Work on a data lake covering 20%+ of the world’s agricultural land, alongside a team of 70+ agriculture, data and tech experts
  • Direct impact on EUDR, DCF and Scope 3 compliance work

How to apply

If this opportunity matches your experience, please apply on Workable:

Your application should include:

  • CV highlighting relevant experience in geospatial data science and machine learning for agricultural applications.
  • A brief proposal (max 3 pages) outlining your approach
  • Examples of previous work
  • Your day rate and availability

jobs.excerpt: Company Introduction:Airspace is a tech-enabled freight forwarder that’s redefining how the world’s most critical packages are delivered.
jobs.description:
Company Introduction:

Airspace is a tech-enabled freight forwarder that’s redefining how the world’s most critical packages are delivered. Headquartered in Carlsbad, California, Airspace has employees who are based around the world. Our European headquarters is in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

As a recognized leader in AI and machine learning, our team leverages data and patented technology to coordinate logistics across a global network of drivers and airlines. Our goal is to deliver those packages that are truly mission-critical in a way that is faster, more transparent, more secure, and more accountable than ever before. The items we deliver range from organs for transplant, to parts for critical machinery including grounded aircraft and highly sensitive components such as semiconductors.

Airspace has been rated one of America’s best Startup Employers and listed as one of CNBC’s Disruptor 50 companies. Airspace has the support of leading investors such as Telstra Ventures, HarbourVest Partners, Defy Partners, DBL Partners, and Scale Ventures. To date the company has raised more than $140m.

The company is growing rapidly and serving more places around the world than ever before. We are looking for passionate, motivated individuals who want to make an IMPACT every day to help us execute on our mission of reshaping the world of time-critical logistics.

Own Consistent Execution Across the Network

You manage two different kinds of leaders. Four Regional Network Managers each own the complete supply picture in their geography, drivers and agents alike, and are accountable for their region’s overall health. Two Agent Leads each own agent-specific execution, onboarding, performance conversations, and (jointly with you and Procurement) deactivation, across two regions apiece. Your job is to make sure standards, tooling, and escalation protocols work the same way across all six of them, and that friction between the RNM and Agent Lead structure never becomes the network’s problem. This role sits at an intersection that’s new to the org: RNMs are accountable for outcomes they don’t personally execute on the agent side, and Agent Leads execute without owning the region they’re executing in. When that split works, neither side notices the seam. When it doesn’t, that’s yours to fix. The most predictable version of this: an Agent Lead covers two regions, and
both RNMs need their attention at once. That’s not a rare edge case, it’s a structural feature of the dotted-line model, and the default answer is you decide the priority when the two RNMs
can’t work it out themselves. You are also one of three required parties, alongside the relevant Agent Lead and Procurement, on every agent deactivation decision. This isn’t a rubber stamp: a deactivation has real consequences for regional coverage, and someone with visibility across all four regions needs to be in that decision, not just the person closest to it.

What You’ll Do

Manage the Regional Network Manager and Agent Lead Teams

  • Directly manage the four Regional Network Managers, owning cross-regional consistency in performance standards, tooling, and escalation protocols
  • Directly manage the two Agent Leads, making sure the two-region split is working, workload is balanced, and agent execution is consistent across all four regions
  • Coach and develop both groups differently — RNMs need broad, general-manager judgment across a full region; Agent Leads need deep, specific judgment on agent performance and the harder conversations that come with it
  • Resolve misalignment between an RNM and the Agent Lead covering their region before it becomes the network’s problem
  • Own prioritization when the two RNMs sharing an Agent Lead both need their attention at the same time — this is a structural, recurring tension with the dotted-line model, not an occasional exception, and the default is that you decide when the RNMs can’t resolve it between

Own Agent Deactivation Decisions

  • Serve as one of three required parties, with the Agent Lead and Procurement, on every agent deactivation decision, bringing the cross-regional and operational perspective an individual Agent Lead may not have
  • Ensure deactivation decisions are documented consistently and held to the same standard across all four regions, not decided differently region by region
  • Escalate to the VP only when a deactivation carries strategic or account-level risk beyond the region it affects

Serve as the Operational Escalation Point

  • Serve as the escalation point for Regional Network Managers on cross-regional issues or decisions that exceed their authority
  • Serve as the escalation point for Agent Leads on issues that cut across more than one region or require senior management-level judgment
  • Stay aligned with the Senior Manager of Network Enablement so recruiting pipelines and training programs reflect regional demand across all four regions.

Partner on Strategic and Cross-Functional Work

  • Partner with the VP on capacity planning, org design, and strategic initiatives for Network Operations
  • Partner with the Director, US Network Solutions during the build phase of new strategic accounts or capabilities, representing what RNMs and Agent Leads actually need to execute cleanly once something is handed off — a bad handoff is a failure regardless of how good the deal was
  • Coordinate with the Lead, US Network Strategy & Operations so the data and scorecard methodology RNMs and Agent Leads depend on is consistent and trustworthy across the network

Requirements

  • 2-5+ years of experience in network operations, field operations, or multi-site operations leadership, with people-management experience across more than one function or team type
  • Experience managing managers, not just individual contributors — comfortable coaching leaders who each own a full geography as well as leaders who own a specialized, narrower function
  • Comfortable being one of three decision-makers on a consequential call rather than the sole decision-maker — shares authority well without diluting accountability
  • Comfortable making a fast, sometimes unpopular prioritization call between two peers who each think their need is more urgent — this happens routinely with a shared Agent Lead, and defaulting to indecision or letting it resolve itself is not an option
  • Strong operational judgment — you can tell the difference between a regional issue that should stay with the RNM and a cross-regional issue that genuinely needs senior management-level intervention
  • Experience partnering with a strategic or business-development-style function receiving handoffs of new capabilities or accounts, and translating them into operational reality on the ground
  • Clear, direct communicator, comfortable resolving disagreements between peers who report to you and who may see a shared problem differently
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Success Metrics

2026

Performance standards, tooling, and escalation protocols are consistent across all four regions. RNMs and Agent Leads report a clear, well-functioning working relationship with each other, not friction that routes to you by default. Agent deactivation decisions are documented consistently and held to the same bar across all four regions. Handoffs from Network Solutions land cleanly, RNMs and Agent Leads report feeling equipped, not blindsided, by new capabilities or accounts.

2027

The RNM and Agent Lead structure is running with enough maturity that it no longer requires your active mediation to function well. Cross-regional consistency in standards and quality is measurably improved. You are spending more time on capacity planning and strategic partnership with the VP and Network Solutions than on resolving day-to-day friction between your direct reports.

Your First 90 Days

Build individual working relationships with all four Regional Network Managers and both Agent Leads. Get fluent in how the RNM and Agent Lead structure is actually working today, where the seams are clean and where they’re not. Sit in on at least one agent deactivation decision to understand how that three-way call is functioning in practice. Build a working relationship with the Director, US Network Solutions and the Lead, US Network Strategy & Operations.

Your First 180 Days

Performance standards and escalation protocols are consistent and well understood across all six direct reports. You have a track record on agent deactivation decisions that RNMs, Agent Leads, and Procurement trust. At least one Network Solutions handoff has gone through cleanly with your involvement from early in the build. The VP sees you as the person keeping regional execution consistent, not just the person four RNMs happen to report to.

Job Info

  • Department: Network
  • Reports to: VP, US Network
  • Location: Remote (U.S.), with periodic travel to support regions and cross-functional handoffs
  • Direct reports: 4 Regional Network Managers, 2 Agent Leads (6 total)

Compensation

  • Salary range: $115K - $125K
  • High-quality health, dental, and vision plan options
  • Open PTO
  • 401K with company match

Core Values:

  • We are One Team. We believe we all accomplish more when we are working together.
  • We make an Impact. We are determined to have a positive influence on our environment, our customers, our industry, and our world.
  • We are Passionate. We care deeply about our mission and are not afraid to raise the bar.
  • We are Transparent. We pride ourselves on having open, honest, and sincere communication with our team and customers.
  • We are Innovative. We never settle and are always striving to improve our product, service, and ourselves.

Airspace is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. Additionally, Airspace participates in the E-Verify program for all locations.

A friendly reminder: Airspace will only contact candidates from an @airspace.com email, a no-reply notification from , or a verified LinkedIn profile. We never request fees or sensitive personal/financial information during recruiting. If something seems suspicious or feels off, please reach out to us at before responding.

Reporting directly to the Head of IT, the IT Manager will oversee, evolve, and secure our core corporate IT infrastructure, platforms, and support services.   • Virtualization & Systems: Administer and optimize core HyperVisors, Active Directory/Domain structures, and overall server health.
  • Network & Security Fabric: Maintain advanced network configurations, firewalls, corporate VPN services, and physical integrations (CCTV and Alarm systems).

Operational Momentum & Availability

  • Incident Ownership: Serve as the final escalation point and incident commander for critical internal IT and infrastructure service disruptions.

  • Process Automation: Partner with your report to eliminate operational bottlenecks by automating routine workflows via Jira, scripts, and internal tooling.

Compliance & Cross-Functional Engagement

  • Regulatory Remediation: Drive regular infrastructure audits and lead technical execution for PCI-DSS remediations and Security/Risk assessment requests.

  • Fintech Literacy: Previous exposure to or hands on management of highly secure processing environments or financial message environments (SWIFT, SEPA, regulatory reporting ecosystems).

Skills & Attributes

  • Strategic Thinker, Practical Doer: Equal capability to design a 3 year modernization roadmap and dive into complex multi system troubleshooting alongside your engineer.

Nice to Have / Advantage

  • Advanced Compliance: Prior experience directly facilitating technical evidence gathering for audits.

Staff Product Security Engineer

Remote: United States, UK, Canada

The role, in a nutshell

At Chainguard, our security posture is our competitive advantage. As a Staff Product Security Engineer, you will help make secure-by-default development a reality across our products and engineering organization.

You will lead high-impact, cross-functional security initiatives; partner closely with Engineering, Product, and Security leadership; and turn complex risks into practical, shippable improvements. A key focus of this role is the AI SDLC: establishing the policies, tooling, and guardrails that enable engineers to use AI responsibly and do the right thing by default—from design and coding through testing, review, deployment, and operations.

This is a hands-on staff-level role for someone who can operate independently, influence multiple teams without direct authority, and raise the security maturity of the organization through both technical execution and strong partnership.

What you’ll do

  • Drive product security strategy and execution across multiple products, platforms, and engineering teams.
  • Lead the evolution of Chainguard’s secure SDLC, with particular emphasis on the AI SDLC and the changing risks of AI-assisted development.
  • Define and implement practical guardrails for AI use in engineering, including secure patterns, policy, workflow controls, review practices, and automation that help teams move quickly while using AI responsibly.
  • Partner with Engineering to embed security controls into the full development lifecycle, including architecture, design, coding, testing, code review, deployment, and operations.
  • Lead secure architecture reviews and threat-modeling efforts for high-impact systems; identify systemic weaknesses early and guide teams toward scalable mitigations.
  • Own cross-functional initiatives such as vulnerability reduction, security automation, and secure-by-default engineering improvements.
  • Partner with Engineering to automate vulnerability detection, triage and remediation, including policy-as-code and cloud or container security controls.
  • Champion the adoption of security tooling—including static and dynamic analysis, dependency and license checks, infrastructure-as-code scanners, and AI-related controls—within developer workflows and CI/CD.
  • Improve how Chainguard runs and consumes security assurance activities such as penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, bug bounty programs, and red-team exercises so findings result in lasting improvements.
  • Translate frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, and SLSA into durable, automation-friendly engineering controls.
  • Stay current on emerging threats, software supply-chain risks, and AI security developments, and turn them into concrete changes to our controls, tooling, and product direction.
  • Influence senior stakeholders through clear risk framing, trade-off analysis, and pragmatic recommendations.
  • Mentor Product Security Engineers and help raise the security bar across the engineering organization.

What we’re looking for

  • 7+ years of experience in software, product, application, or cloud security.
  • Experience driving security programs from design through rollout, such as secure SDLC, AI SDLC, vulnerability management, platform hardening, or security automation.
  • Practical understanding of how engineers build and ship software, with the ability to translate security requirements into workflows teams will adopt.
  • Strong hands-on familiarity with containers, Kubernetes, public cloud, and associated security controls.
  • Experience with security compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, or SLSA, and the ability to translate controls into practical engineering work.
  • Ability to automate security workflows in at least one language, such as Go, Python, or Shell, and integrate them into CI/CD.
  • Proven ability to influence and align teams through clear, concise communication in a remote-first environment.
  • Strong ownership, accountability, and adaptability—you anticipate risks, navigate ambiguity, and leave systems and teams better than you found them.   • Background in software supply-chain security, including SBOMs,, provenance, signing, or build-system hardening.
  • Experience with red-teaming, offensive security, or security-sensitive open-source software development.
  • Experience with SAST, DAST, SCA, IaC scanning, policy-as-code, or related security tooling.

jobs.excerpt: WHO WE ARE American Oversight (AO) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit watchdog that advances truth, accountability, and democracy by enforcing the public’s right to government records.
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

American Oversight (AO) is a nonpartisan, nonprofit watchdog that advances truth, accountability, and democracy by enforcing the public’s right to government records. We use multiple tools, backed by aggressive litigation, to fight attacks on democratic institutions, threats to civil rights and liberties, abuses of power, and the erosion of government transparency. We expose and disrupt these attacks — and the officials and networks behind them — by forcing the government to turn over records officials would rather keep secret.

Since our founding in 2017, American Oversight has worked on issues that touch nearly every aspect of American life. Our team has:

  • Secured a court order to preserve records in the 2025 “Signalgate” scandal, and spurred a related investigation by the Department of Defense inspector general that found Secretary Pete Hegseth had put troops’ lives in danger and violated federal recordkeeping laws.
  • Forced DOGE to implement a records preservation policy to ensure long-term accountability for its chaotic actions.
  • Revealed the Trump-sanctioned pressure campaign on the Ukrainian government by forcing the Trump administration to turn over records initially withheld from Congress.
  • Unmasked sham “audits” of the 2020 election in Wisconsin and Arizona, which used taxpayer money to undermine state elections.
  • Exposed the Trump administration’s unprecedented use of personal data to target immigrant communities and remove people from state voter rolls.

We are committed to fighting threats to democracy at the federal, state, and local levels, using time-tested and innovative tools to expose misconduct, defend against attacks on marginalized communities, and demand accountability.

For more information, please visit our website:

JOB OVERVIEW

The Director of Partnerships and Strategic Initiatives is a key member of American Oversight’s leadership team, responsible for shaping and executing the organization’s vision for partnerships and external engagement. The Director identifies, initiates, and cultivates strategic relationships that expand American Oversight’s influence and position it as the nation’s leading public records watchdog.

The Director builds and sustains mission-aligned partnerships that strengthen American Oversight’s sustainability and amplify its long-term impact across the progressive movement. By ensuring that the organization’s investigative findings and records reach partners, coalitions, policymakers, and other stakeholders best positioned to act on them, the Director helps translate American Oversight’s work into broader policy impact and systemic change.

Internally, the Director works closely with executive leadership and the Development team, and collaborates across the legal, communications, editorial, and investigations teams to ensure the organization’s work achieves maximum reach, strategic coordination, and measurable impact.

RESPONSIBILITIES (including but not limited to)

Partnerships and External Engagement

  • Direct American Oversight’s partnerships and external engagement strategy to expand the organization’s influence and cement American Oversight as the go-to authority on the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) and public records work across the progressive movement at the federal, state, and local levels.
  • Strengthen American Oversight’s reputation as a trusted leader in government transparency, using strategic partnerships to identify high-impact investigations, litigation, and communications strategies designed to expose misconduct, expand public access to information, drive accountability, and support democratic progress.
  • Set and lead American Oversight’s strategic partnership priorities, building relationships with organizations whose complementary strengths, networks, and connections to impacted communities advance shared goals and broaden collective impact.
  • Proactively monitor and analyze political and policy dynamics at the federal, state, and local levels, cultivating partner insights to surface emerging threats and opportunities that guide American Oversight’s strategic direction and advance democratic accountability.
  • Develop and lead coalition-based strategies that leverage American Oversight’s expertise and records to shape accountability efforts, advance advocacy campaigns, and defend democratic institutions — including by drafting or supporting sign-on letters, joint statements, and other collaborative initiatives that amplify collective advocacy and align with American Oversight’s strategic priorities.
  • Facilitate webinars, presentations, and other public-facing engagements that showcase American Oversight’s findings, elevate the organization’s expertise, and strengthen relationships with partners, policymakers, and funders.
  • Elevate American Oversight’s visibility and influence across the accountability and democracy ecosystem by identifying, recommending, and securing opportunities for organizational leadership to participate in high-impact conferences, coalitions, and convenings that enhance the organization’s reputation and amplify its impact.
  • Advise executive leadership on strategic positioning within the broader progressive and democracy ecosystem, including assessing and managing potential risks in partnerships and coalitions.
  • Serve as American Oversight’s senior representative to external partners, coalitions, and public forums, advancing the organization’s mission, amplifying its priorities, and strengthening its credibility and influence across the accountability ecosystem.
Strategic Operations and Leadership
  • Translate broad organizational priorities into actionable partnership and strategic initiative plans, establishing milestones, coordinating internal contributions, and taking responsibility for execution and follow-through.
  • Define and track key performance metrics to evaluate the reach, influence, and effectiveness of American Oversight’s strategic engagement, ensuring accountability for outcomes and progress toward strategic goals.
  • Oversee American Oversight’s Client Relationship Management and Partnerships systems to ensure data hygiene, efficient information flow, and measurable tracking of partnerships growth and external engagement impact.
  • Build organizational capacity for external engagement by coaching and training staff across departments to effectively represent American Oversight in partnerships, coalitions, and public forums.
  • Coach and mentor direct report(s) by setting clear performance expectations, providing regular feedback, and supporting skills development and professional growth to strengthen individual and team effectiveness.
  • Other duties as assigned.
Development and Fundraising
  • Support American Oversight’s development and sustainability efforts by collaborating with executive leadership to design, execute, and sustain fundraising strategies, engage funders, and cultivate relationships.
  • Collaborate with the Development and Communications teams to translate American Oversight’s partnerships, impact, and investigations into compelling narratives that inspire donor engagement and investment.
  • Assist with or draft grant and impact reports, as well as other funder-facing materials, that communicate American Oversight’s achievements and reinforce relationships with institutional supporters.
  • Ensure alignment between external engagement initiatives and development priorities, leveraging partnerships, events, and visibility opportunities to advance fundraising goals and institutional relationships.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Position Summary

Uneekor, Inc. uses technology and design to connect the world through golf, empowering every golfer to be the best version of themselves on and off the course. We have revolutionized the US golf simulator industry from the commercial golf simulator market success at the global level by offering first-of-its-kind overhead launch monitors in the open technology platform to thousands of individual golfers. Seamlessly combining hardware and simulator software programs, our passion is to create valuable content, products, and services that fulfill millions of golfers’ passion for their love of the game.

We are seeking an Ecommerce Specialist to support the day-to-day management and execution of our ecommerce business across D2C, B2B, and international markets.

This role will work primarily within Shopify and Sanity CMS to manage products, merchandising, website content, promotions, and ecommerce operations. This role will also serve as a key content manager for Uneekor’s international websites, ensuring regional experiences remain accurate, current, and aligned with the brand.

The ideal candidate combines hands-on ecommerce experience with an understanding of digital marketing principles and a strong technical aptitude. We are looking for someone who is proactive, self-sufficient, comfortable taking ownership of projects, and interested in growing their responsibilities as Uneekor’s digital commerce business expands.

Responsibilities

Ecommerce & Merchandising

  • Manage the day-to-day administration of Uneekor’s Shopify environment across D2C, B2B, and international markets.
  • Create and maintain products, variants, bundles, SIMKITs, collections, pricing, availability, promotions, and merchandising.
  • Maintain accurate product information, specifications, imagery, metadata, SKUs, and other ecommerce data.
  • Support ecommerce execution for product launches, promotions, B2B programs, and international expansion.
  • Maintain Shopify Markets, catalogs, company configurations, shipping settings, product availability, and other ecommerce rules.
  • Identify opportunities to improve merchandising, customer experience, and operational efficiency.

Website & Content Management

  • Manage and publish website content through Shopify and Sanity CMS, including PDPs, collections, landing pages, navigation, and promotional content.
  • Serve as a content manager for Uneekor’s international websites, maintaining regional content, imagery, navigation, promotions, and product information.
  • Coordinate localization and translation needs across international markets.
  • Apply ecommerce and digital marketing principles to how products, promotions, and content are presented throughout the customer journey.
  • Ensure consistency between ecommerce data and customer-facing website content.

Ecommerce Operations & QA

  • Monitor the storefront for product, pricing, content, checkout, navigation, and functionality issues.
  • Perform QA for website updates, promotions, product launches, integrations, and platform changes across desktop and mobile.
  • Troubleshoot ecommerce and website issues independently, identifying whether issues are related to content, configuration, integrations, or development.
  • Coordinate with internal and external technical resources when development support is required.
  • Support implementation of approved SEO, analytics, and conversion improvements.
  • Manage ecommerce data through imports, exports, bulk updates, and other catalog management processes.
  • Document key ecommerce configurations and processes and identify opportunities to automate or simplify recurring workflows.

Cross-Functional Support

  • Work closely with Digital Commerce, Marketing, Product, Sales, Customer Experience, Operations, and Engineering.
  • Translate business requirements into ecommerce and website execution.
  • Coordinate with Operations on inventory, fulfillment, shipping, and product availability requirements.
  • Support external agencies and development partners with ecommerce requirements, testing, and QA.
  • Take ownership of assigned projects and follow them through to completion with limited day-to-day oversight.

Qualifications, Knowledge & Critical Skills

  • 3+ years of ecommerce or digital commerce experience, preferably with hands-on Shopify experience.
  • Experience managing ecommerce products, merchandising, promotions, and website content.
  • Working knowledge of digital marketing principles, including customer journey, conversion, SEO, promotions, and content merchandising.
  • Experience working with a CMS; Sanity experience is a plus.
  • Experience with Shopify Markets, international ecommerce, or Shopify B2B is a plus.
  • Experience working with ecommerce data, CSV imports/exports, bulk product updates, or catalog management tools.
  • Experience with HTML/CSS, web development, APIs, ecommerce integrations, or other technical web concepts is a plus, but not required.
  • Comfortable learning new platforms and understanding how ecommerce systems and integrations work together.
  • Strong attention to detail, organization, written communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proactive and self-sufficient, with the ability to identify what needs to be done and take ownership through completion.
  • Strong desire to learn, take on additional responsibility, and grow within the Digital Commerce team.
  • Knowledge of golf, golf technology, launch monitors, or the golf simulator industry is preferred.

  • Partner with Analytics to establish channel specific targets.
  • Build, launch, manage, and optimize campaigns across platforms such as Meta, TikTok, programmatic, DSPs, and mobile ad networks.
  • Make disciplined investment decisions based on business objectives and performance metrics, including CPA, ROAS, LTV, and payback period.
  • Manage and hold agencies, partners, and technology vendors accountable for execution quality, and business results.
  • Identify, test, and scale new acquisition channels, platforms, audiences, and partnerships.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years in user acquisition, performance marketing, or growth marketing.
  • Proven track record managing significant paid media budgets against CPA, ROAS, LTV, and payback targets.
  • Hands on expertise across Meta, programmatic, DSPs, mobile ad networks, and ASO including audience setup, bidding, attribution, and optimization.
  • Strong grasp of mobile attribution (SKAdNetwork, MMPs like AppsFlyer) and privacy-related measurement limits.
  • Strong leadership and communication skills manages people, agencies, and stakeholders, and turns data into clear decisions.

Job Summary:

The mission of the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is to advance the public's health through learning, discovery and communication. To pursue the mission, the school produces knowledge through research then translates this knowledge into evidence that can be communicated to the public, policymakers, and practitioners to advance the health of populations.

The Office of Sponsored Programs Administration (SPA) supports the School's mission by serving as a central resource for the research community through the provision of expertise and leadership in obtaining and managing research funds. It acts as the institutional representative of the President and Fellows of Harvard College for the administration of sponsored projects for the school. SPA is comprised of research administrators that work in partnership with faculty to review and submit proposals for funding and to ensure that proposals and then awards conform and are managed according to sponsor guidelines and University policies.

The Associate Director of Finance (ADF) supports innovative research at the world’s leading public health research institution, working across the Department of Environmental Health and the Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies (HCPDS). The Department of Environmental Health advances environmental health through hands-on learning, evidence -based research, and translation of discoveries into actions that reduce harmful exposures and improve health, with longstanding strengths in the epidemiology of cancer, cardiovascular, and other chronic diseases. It also educates and prepares future medical and public health leaders. Administered by the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, the Harvard Center for Population and Development Studies (HCPDS) brings together scientists from across the University to make critical advances in population research. With over 70 affiliated faculty from the Kennedy School of Government, the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, the Medical School, and other schools, HCPDS is a University-wide, interdisciplinary center dedicated to understanding how demographic change and social and physical environments shape global population health.

The Associate Director of Finance is a key departmental leader responsible for overall financial and grants management. This role supervises a team of financial staff, including grant managers and accounts payable personnel. The position reports to the Director of Finance, Administration, and Compliance in Sponsored Programs Administration, with joint reporting lines to the Director of Administration (EH) and the Deputy Director (HCPDS).

The Associate Director of Finance is an integral part of the research enterprise and works in close partnership with faculty members to advise them on the financial management of their funds and will have oversight over the Department's sponsored research portfolio as well as their non sponsored funds.

    • Supervising and training research and financial administrators; providing daily guidance
    • Allocating workloads to maximize research administrator effectiveness
    • Assessing performance and conducting reviews for staff

    • Developing and implementing departmental policies and processes
    • Ensuring research administration compliance with sponsor guidelines and Harvard policies
    • Ensuring departmental financial transactions are compliant with Harvard and sponsor policies and regulations; approves and transmits most departmental transactions.
  • Strategic and Financial Leadership
    • Oversight and management of the department’s non-sponsored accounts. These include but are not limited to endowments, gifts, start-up funding, and cost recovery centers
    • Collaborates with departments academic staff regarding student finances and financial planning
    • Preparing annual Department budget, working closely with the Department Administrator and senior leadership
    • Working closely with senior management, including the Director of Administration, Department Chair, and Directors of educational programs and student services, in developing and implementing strategic financial plans
    • Participating in School-wide and University-wide initiatives and meetings
  • Performs other duties as assigned

  • Minimum of 7 years’ relevant work experience
  • Advanced knowledge of sponsored research regulations
  • Supervisory experience

  • MBA or Masters’ degree in relevant field
  • CRA certification
  • Strong computing skills, particularly with Microsoft Excel and Word
  • Experience with Microsoft Office Suite, advanced Excel skills

About CustomerGauge

CustomerGauge is the B2B account experience platform trusted by global enterprises to measure, act on, and monetize customer feedback. We help companies reduce churn, grow revenue, and build lasting customer loyalty through Net Promoter Score and account experience programs. Our customers include some of the world's most recognized brands across manufacturing, distribution, technology, and professional services.

The Role

We're looking for a presales solutions principal to serve as CustomerGauge's technical trusted advisor to mid-market and enterprise prospects across Europe and North America and occasionally farther afield. You'll own the technical and CX-program side of complex, high-value sales cycles, earning the confidence of buyers through deep NPS and CX domain expertise, hands-on solution architecture, and a consultative approach that sets CustomerGauge apart from the competition.

This is a deal-winning role. You'll partner with account executives from the first discovery call through technical close, and you'll be the person prospects trust to tell them how a program should be designed, how the platform fits their data and systems landscape, and what it will take to deliver measurable business outcomes.

You'll report to the CRO.

What You'll Do

  • Bring genuine NPS and CX domain expertise into every conversation, connecting platform capabilities directly to measurable business outcomes that matter to the buyer
  • Own the technical and CX-program side of sales cycles: lead discovery, solution architecture, proof-of-concept engagements, demonstrations, and executive presentations
  • Partner closely with the sales team to shape, qualify, and accelerate deals from a technical and domain standpoint, positioning CustomerGauge as the clear, credible choice
  • Translate complex business and technical requirements into solution designs that hold up under scrutiny: integration architecture, data flows, program configuration, and implementation approach
  • Lead responses to RFPs, RFIs, and security questionnaires; run technical deep-dives with IT, data, and operations stakeholders, drawing on expert team members as needed
  • Design and deliver tailored demos and proofs of concept that reflect each prospect's industry, data, and program goals
  • Engage at all levels of the prospect organization, from IT architects and program owners to the C-suite, with equal fluency
  • Hand off closed deals cleanly to services and account management with a clear record of scope, solution design, and success criteria
  • Feed competitive intelligence and prospect requirements back to product and marketing to sharpen positioning and inform the roadmap
  • Continuously develop demo environments, reference architectures, and presales assets that raise the bar for the wider sales team
  • Extend the same in support of our customer Account Management team, i.e., work with existing customers on occasion in expansion sales pursuits.

What We're Looking For

  • 3-5+ years of experience in presales solutions consulting or sales engineering, ideally in B2B SaaS
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in NPS, customer experience measurement, or customer feedback programs; this is required, not a bonus. Experience with Voice of the Customer (VoC) program design and implementation
  • Proven ability to lead complex technical sales cycles at the enterprise level: solution architecture, integration design, RFP responses, and proof-of-concept engagements
  • Demonstrated track record as a technical trusted advisor whose counsel prospects seek on architecture, program design, and strategy

Benefits

  • Participation in the SAR Plan

Vår vision är att vara den absolut bästa arbetsgivaren för en skicklig och ambitiös IT-konsult. Därför lägger vi stor vikt vid dig då du är det viktigaste vi har. Ja, vem är du? Vad vill du göra? Vad brinner du för? Vi arbetar fram det uppdrag som går i linje med din plan för framtiden. Om du inte har någon plan så fixar vi en tillsammans!

Vi ser gärna att du har några års arbetslivserfarenhet efter dina studier från något tekniskt universitet. Sannolikt är du systemvetare eller ingenjör. Viktigast är dock att du är en relationsbyggande person som trivs i konsultrollen.

Hos oss får du roliga uppdrag som du själv är med och styr över. Kompetensutveckling öser vi över dig och den är naturligtvis betald och individuell. Kulturen är inkluderande och förutom fast lön har vi även marknadens bästa förmånspaket (ja, vi benchmarkar).

Vill du också arbeta på Sveriges bästa arbetsplats?

Ansök då med att fylla i formuläret nedan, men innan dess så kan det vara bra att veta, att intervjuerna sker på svenska så vi förutsätter att du behärskar det väl i både tal och skrift.

Technosylva has provided critical solutions for the past 26 years. In 2024 General Atlantic, a leading global growth investor, announced a strategic growth investment in Technosylva to support the company in its mission.

Role Overview

We are hiring a backend-focused Senior Software Engineer to build and optimize the high-performance services and compute models at the core of our platform. This role combines strong systems and backend engineering with advanced numerical and parallel-computing expertise. You will design robust services and APIs while also writing the highly optimized, concurrent code that makes large-scale simulation fast and accurate. It is an ideal fit for an engineer who is equally comfortable reasoning about service architecture and squeezing performance out of compute- and memory-intensive workloads.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and maintain backend services and APIs (REST/gRPC or equivalent).
  • Model, optimize, and maintain relational and non-relational databases — schema design, query tuning, and data integrity.
  • Implement and troubleshoot inter-process communication (IPC, messaging, and service-to-service protocols).
  • Develop primary backend systems in C# and Java.
  • Design and implement highly optimized compute models in C++.
  • Apply synchronization, concurrency, and multi-processing techniques to maximize throughput and correctness.
  • Profile, benchmark, and optimize performance-critical code paths.
  • Translate mathematical and algorithmic requirements into efficient, production-grade code.
  • Participate in architecture decisions, code reviews, and technical mentorship.
  • Write clean, testable, well-documented code and contribute to CI/CD practices.

Requirements

Required

  • Strong proficiency in C# and Java for backend development.
  • Strong C++ skills for high-performance compute work.
  • Solid understanding of concurrency, synchronization primitives, threading, and multi-processing.
  • Strong mathematical proficiency — numerical methods, linear algebra, or applied math relevant to compute models.
  • Experience with API design, database design, and IPC mechanisms.
  • Proven ability to profile and optimize compute- and memory-intensive workloads.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with parallel and high-performance computing — multithreading at scale, SIMD/vectorization, GPU (CUDA/OpenCL), or distributed compute (MPI).

Overview: Multi-Tenant Cloud Infrastructure Design

The Cloud Architect is responsible for designing, managing, and optimizing the entire multi-tenant cloud infrastructure that hosts our integrated supply chain e-commerce platform. While our current stack utilizes Oracle Cloud Free VMs, this role requires expertise in major public clouds (AWS/GCP/Azure) to architect scalable, resilient, cost-optimized, and compliant solutions that handle fluctuating e-commerce traffic, stable internal tool usage, and intensive AI agent compute demands.

Internship Details

Duration: 3 months

Start Date: Immediate

Location: Remote

Stipend: None initially. Based on your first-quarter performance, you may be offered a paid full-time opportunity, or even be absorbed directly by the client as an FTE.

Key Responsibilities & Core Projects

You will design and govern the platform's foundation, ensuring scalability and compliance across all environments.

  • Cloud Architecture Design: Design and evolve the target cloud infrastructure (utilizing AWS, GCP, or Azure best practices) for maximum scalability, security, and high-availability, ensuring the platform can reliably support the MES $\rightarrow$ WMS $\rightarrow$ OMS flow.

  • Capacity Planning & Optimization: Plan and optimize resource allocation to effectively handle unpredictable e-commerce traffic spikes and the specific compute requirements for AI agent training and inference, driving cost efficiency.

  • High Availability & Disaster Recovery (DR): Implement multi-region/multi-AZ high-availability architectures and define comprehensive Disaster Recovery (DR) strategies for all core services, including PostgreSQL 15 and Redis.

  • Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Governance: Establish and enforce best practices for Terraform usage, ensuring configuration consistency, security compliance, and auditable infrastructure changes.

  • Security & Compliance: Conduct regular security reviews of cloud configurations (e.g., IAM, VPC/VNet, Storage) and ensure architecture aligns with data residency and compliance requirements relevant to our multi-tenant operations.

  • Service Integration: Architect the network and service mesh overlay that integrates the containerized applications (Docker/Traefik) with external cloud services and the overall monitoring solution (Prometheus, OpenTelemetry).

Required Technologies & Tools

Candidates must possess deep architectural experience with public cloud providers and infrastructure automation:

  • Cloud Providers: Expert-level proficiency in at least one major public cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

  • Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC): Mandatory expertise in Terraform for cloud resource provisioning.

  • Containerization: Deep knowledge of Docker networking, security, and orchestration principles.

  • Networking & Edge: Experience configuring load balancing, service mesh, and ingress controllers (e.g., Traefik).

  • Data & Storage: Architecting scalable database services (PostgreSQL) and object storage (MinIO).

  • Security: Cloud security best practices, IAM policy design, and network segmentation.

AI Agent Focus

You will optimize the cloud layer for our emerging AI capabilities.

  • Compute Optimization: Design elastic and cost-effective compute clusters (e.g., GPU instances) to efficiently handle the variable demands of LLM fine-tuning and multi-agent system orchestration.

  • Data Residency: Architect the data pipeline and storage solutions to ensure that training data and model artifacts adhere to strict data residency requirements across tenants.

Success Metrics & Career Path

Performance will be measured by:

  • Cost Efficiency: Demonstrable reduction in cloud operational costs (FinOps) while maintaining performance.

  • Availability: Achieving defined SLAs/SLOs for infrastructure uptime and performance.

  • Compliance: Successful implementation and auditing of cloud security and data residency controls.

Mentorship Structure: Reports to the Solution Architect or Head of Technology, collaborating closely with the SRE and DevSecOps teams to operationalize cloud strategy.

About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Available Locations: Austin, San Francisco

Principal, GTM Automation, RevOps

What We're Looking For:

We're hiring a Principal for GTM Automation to document processes, build the AI agents and automation, and design improvements for our Revenue organization (Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Partner, RevOps). This is a senior individual contributor role where you will build and maintain the automation needed to drive efficiency and reduce operational friction.

The hard part of this job is knowing where not to put an agent. You'll decide which parts of prospecting, account research, deal management, and renewals can be handed to AI systems, where a person has to stay involved, and how we confirm the output is right before a seller acts on it. You will work directly with Sales leadership, Revenue Operations, Enablement, and the data and engineering teams on tools that save sellers real time. Success is identified by creating systems that resolve mundane tasks and save people real time. We are looking for someone who has run agentic systems in production for a business team and can tell us what broke and what they changed.

Location: Remote, Austin or San Francisco

What You'll Get To Do In This Role:

  • Design and build agentic workflows for repetitive revenue work such as account creation and enrichment, CRM updates, renewals, QBR prep, deal registration, account ownership, etc. Add RBAC, observability, error handling, etc. to make the systems as robust as possible.
  • Decide where AI and automation fit in the go-to-market motion, and where human judgment is still required.
  • Set the quality bar for agents in production: evals that run before every release, monitoring tied to pipeline and revenue, clear rules for sensitive data, and a tested rollback.
  • Own the architecture that connects agents to Salesforce, the data warehouse, enrichment and intent sources, and call data, so the next workflow reuses what the last one built.
  • Build the signal layer that feeds account prioritization, routing, and next-best-action. Product usage, intent, firmographic changes, and call transcripts all go in.
  • Review code and designs from stakeholders (analysts, Revenue Operations partners, etc.). Where version control, tests, or code review are missing, help put them in place.
  • Work with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success leaders to find the work worth automating, and say no to the work that isn't. Measure adoption and business impact for everything that ships. Retire tools that the organization isn’t using.
  • Track new models, agent frameworks, and vendor tools, and decide what's worth adopting.
  • Document each system and who owns it, so it keeps running when you move on to the next one.

What We're Looking For In You:

  • 10+ years in software engineering, data engineering, GTM automation, or revenue systems, with several years owning systems from design through production support at staff level or above.
  • At least one LLM-powered workflow or agent that a business team relied on in production. Be ready to walk us through how it called tools, handled failures, and was evaluated.
  • Strong Python or TypeScript, and strong SQL. You write tested code, and you can review AI-generated code well enough to catch what it gets wrong.
  • Hands-on Salesforce experience with the data model, Flow, APIs, and permissions, and a clear sense of how CRM data goes bad when automation writes to it. Comfort working directly in BigQuery, Snowflake, or a similar warehouse.
  • Experience integrating SaaS systems over REST APIs and webhooks, and tracing a failure back to its source.
  • Working knowledge of enrichment and signal tools such as D&B, ZoomInfo, and HG Insights, and a view on what to do when two sources disagree.
  • You can explain the same system to a sales VP in two sentences and to an engineer in a schema, and you can influence leaders on teams that don't report to you.

  • Lead autotest coverage. Set coverage and priorities for the autotest engineer, and write or fix tests yourself when needed.

About the role

As a Technical Support Engineer at a pioneering AI company, you'll be the first line of defense to support customers as they build out training, fine tuning, and inference solutions with Together AI. You'll dive deep into complex technical challenges, providing swift and effective solutions while serving as a product expert. As a part of the Customer Experience organization, you will collaborate closely with product and sales, driving continuous improvement of our offerings. This is an exciting opportunity for a deeply technical professional passionate about AI and customer success to make a significant impact in a fast-paced, innovative environment.

Required hours

  • This is a fulltime position working US daytime hours. The role will work both weekend days (Saturday and Sunday) as well as two additional weekdays.
  • This is a 4-day shift, 10 hours per day, with 2 additional hours of on-call coverage on Saturdays and Sundays.
  • The role would start as a Monday to Friday role for the first few months to allow for ramping up and learning from teammates. After being considered fully ramped, the role would transition to the 4-day weekend shift.

Responsibilities

  • Engage directly with customers to tackle and resolve complex technical challenges involving our cutting-edge Kubernetes GPU clusters; ensure swift and effective solutions every time.
  • Act as a customer facing SRE to ensure our customer’s Kubernetes clusters remain healthy and stable
  • Become a product expert in our GPU Cluster service, serving as the last line of technical defense before issues are escalated to Engineering and Product teams.
  • Monitor GPU cluster health and proactively communicate hardware issues to customers (thermal throttling, BMC failures, missing GPUs, and NVLink/InfiniBand degradation) with clear remediation steps
  • Operate and maintain production infrastructure for enterprise GPU customers, including fleet rebalancing, Slurm cluster maintenance, node repair/migration, and Kubernetes-based workload management
  • Investigate and resolve storage and networking issues such as Weka filesystem degradation, InfiniBand link failures, and bandwidth anomalies on bare-metal and VM environments
  • Collaborate seamlessly across Engineering, Research, and Product teams to address customer concerns; collaborate with senior leaders both internally and externally to ensure the highest levels of customer satisfaction.
  • Transform customer insights into action by identifying patterns in support cases and working with Engineering and Go-To-Market teams to drive Together’s roadmap (e.g., future models to support)
  • Maintain detailed documentation of system configurations, procedures, troubleshooting guides, and FAQs to facilitate knowledge sharing with team and customers.
  • Be flexible in providing support coverage during holidays, nights and weekends as required by business needs to ensure consistent and reliable service for our customers.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in a customer-facing technical role with at least 1 year in a support function for an AI service or supporting a mission-critical API in SaaS
  • Experience as an SRE or DevOps engineer working with Kubernetes
  • Strong technical background, with knowledge of AI, ML, GPU technologies and their integration into high-performance computing (HPC) environments.
  • Advanced knowledge with infrastructure services (e.g., Kubernetes, SLURM), infrastructure as code solutions (e.g., Ansible) high-performance network fabrics, NFS-based storage management, container infrastructure, and scripting and programming languages.
  • Experience with HPC/Slurm cluster environments — node draining, job scheduling, maintenance workflows
  • Familiarity with high-speed networking concepts — InfiniBand, RDMA, network interface diagnostics
  • Experience with distributed storage systems (e.g., Weka, NFS) and troubleshooting I/O and bandwidth issues
  • Foundational understanding in the installation, configuration, administration, troubleshooting, and securing of compute clusters.
  • Complex technical problem solving and troubleshooting, with a proactive approach to issue resolution
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with teams such as Sales, Engineering, Support, Product and Research to drive customer success.
  • Strong sense of ownership and willingness to learn new skills to ensure both team and customer success.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to operate in dynamic environments, adept at managing multiple projects, and comfortable with frequent context switching and prioritization.

About Together AI

Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month.

Compensation

We offer competitive compensation, startup equity, health insurance, and other benefits, as well as flexibility in terms of remote work. The US base salary range for this full-time position is: $160K - $230K + equity + benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by location, level and role. Individual compensation will be determined by experience, skills, and job-related knowledge.

Equal Opportunity

Together AI is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is proud to offer equal employment opportunity to everyone regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, and more.
