jobs.excerpt: Mirantis, an IREN company, is the Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure company, enabling organizations to build and operate scalable, secure, and sovereign infrastructure for modern AI, machine learning, and data-intensive applications.
jobs.description:
Mirantis, an IREN company, is the Kubernetes-native AI infrastructure company, enabling organizations to build and operate scalable, secure, and sovereign infrastructure for modern AI, machine learning, and data-intensive applications. By combining open-source innovation with deep expertise in Kubernetes orchestration, Mirantis empowers platform engineering teams to deliver composable, production-ready developer platforms across any environment — on-premises, in the cloud, at the edge, or in sovereign data centers.

As enterprises navigate the growing complexity of AI-driven workloads, Mirantis delivers the automation, GPU orchestration, and policy-driven control needed to manage infrastructure with confidence and agility. Committed to open standards and freedom from lock-in, Mirantis ensures that customers retain full control of their infrastructure strategy.

Job Description

We are looking for an experienced DevOps Engineer to own the deployment, release, and reliability backbone of the k0rdent-ai platform — our multi-tenant control plane for enterprise GPU infrastructure. The platform’s core services — identity (Keycloak), API gateway (Kong), workflow engine (Temporal), a suite of Go APIs, and the PostgreSQL databases behind them — run on every control-plane and regional cluster we operate, and must be upgraded safely, observed continuously, and recovered quickly.

You will run this platform across both cloud Kubernetes (AWS) and bare-metal clusters in our data centers, delivering it through Helm charts and k0rdent ServiceTemplates and MultiClusterServices. Beyond day-to-day operations, a substantial focus of this role is engineering the foundations that stateful services depend on: snapshot-capable storage (CSI drivers, StorageClasses, volume snapshots), CloudNativePG backups and point-in-time recovery, and the CI/CD and bare-metal end-to-end pipelines that validate every change before it reaches customers.

Because this platform holds the record of every tenant, user, and cluster action, this role also owns its operational readiness — runbooks, restore drills, and the upgrade and rollback paths that keep a failed release from turning into data loss.

Main Responsibilities

  • Multi-Environment Kubernetes Operations: Deploy, upgrade, and operate k0s / k0rdent-managed Kubernetes clusters on AWS and on bare-metal hardware, across a global control plane and multiple regions — cluster lifecycle, node maintenance, capacity planning, and version upgrades.

  • Helm & Service Delivery: Author and maintain Helm charts and k0rdent ServiceTemplates and MultiClusterServices for core services (Keycloak, Kong, Temporal, CloudNativePG, and in-house Go APIs), including dependency ordering, health gating, versioning, and zero-downtime upgrade paths.

  • Storage & Snapshot Engineering: Design and run Kubernetes storage for each environment — AWS EBS CSI in the cloud; OpenEBS LocalPV, Longhorn, or Ceph on bare metal — including StorageClasses, reclaim policies, the CSI snapshot controller, and VolumeSnapshotClasses, so stateful services can be snapshotted and restored reliably.

  • Database Backup & Recovery: Operate CloudNativePG backup and recovery end to end — scheduled volume snapshots, continuous WAL archiving to object storage, point-in-time recovery, and replica clusters — with defined RPO/RTO targets and regular restore drills.

  • CI/CD & End-to-End Testing: Build and maintain GitHub Actions pipelines for linting, chart unit tests, artifact packaging and publishing to OCI registries, and on-demand bare-metal end-to-end environments; keep them fast, reliable, and easy to debug.

  • GitOps & Infrastructure as Code: Maintain a strictly declarative infrastructure-as-code (IaC) culture using Terraform and Argo CD (or Flux), keeping every environment — from developer labs to production — reproducible and reviewable through code.

  • Observability & Incident Response: Build monitoring and alerting (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry) for service health, database replication and backup status, and capacity; join the on-call rotation, lead troubleshooting, and drive post-incident improvements.

  • Security & Air-Gapped Delivery: Manage TLS and certificate lifecycle (cert-manager), secrets, network policies, and least-privilege RBAC, and support private-registry and air-gapped installations for sovereign customers.

Qualifications

Must Have

  • Platform Experience: 8+ years in DevOps, SRE, or platform engineering, including 3+ years operating production Kubernetes for business-critical services.

  • Kubernetes Depth: Strong grasp of Kubernetes primitives — workloads and StatefulSets, operators and CRDs, persistent volumes and CSI storage, RBAC, and network policies — with hands-on experience upgrading and troubleshooting clusters in production.

  • Helm & Release Engineering: Hands-on authoring of non-trivial Helm charts — templating, values design, chart dependencies, and testing with helm-unittest or chart-testing. Experience with k0rdent, Cluster API, or a multi-cluster delivery tool (Argo CD ApplicationSets, Fleet, Sveltos) is preferred, but what matters is depth with Helm, not the specific delivery tool.

  • Kubernetes Storage: Practical experience with CSI drivers, StorageClasses, and volume snapshots — AWS EBS CSI preferred, but equivalent experience with Longhorn, Ceph (Rook), OpenEBS, or another cloud CSI driver is acceptable. What matters is understanding how storage behaves when pods, nodes, and clusters fail.

  • PostgreSQL on Kubernetes: Hands-on experience running PostgreSQL through a Kubernetes operator — CloudNativePG (CNPG) preferred, but Zalando’s postgres-operator, Crunchy PGO, or a comparable operator is acceptable — including backups, restores, and point-in-time recovery.

  • Cloud Infrastructure: Production experience in AWS (EC2, EBS, VPC, IAM, S3; EKS a plus); equivalent GCP or Azure experience also counts.

  • CI/CD & Automation: Designing and maintaining GitHub Actions (or GitLab CI) pipelines, with solid scripting in Bash plus Python or Go (Golang).

  • Collaboration: Clear written and spoken English and comfort working across time zones, with regular overlap with US and European teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with bare-metal provisioning (Metal3, Ironic, PXE) and GPU or AI infrastructure.

  • Familiarity with Kong Gateway or the Kubernetes Gateway API, and Keycloak / OIDC identity integration.

  • Experience operating Temporal or other workflow engines in production.

  • Experience delivering software into air-gapped or sovereign environments using private registries and mirrored artifacts.

  • Experience designing cross-region disaster recovery for stateful services, including RPO/RTO trade-off decisions.

  • Certifications such as CKA / CKS or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional — a plus.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects (Helm charts, Kubernetes operators, CNCF projects) — a huge plus.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science & Engineering (or a related field), or 8+ years of equivalent related experience.

We offer:

  • Operate some of the most advanced AI infrastructure environments in production today.
  • Work with the latest NVIDIA GPU technologies, Kubernetes platforms, and high-performance networking environments.
  • Help define operational standards and reliability practices for next-generation AI infrastructure services.
  • Influence the adoption of AI-powered operational capabilities through k0rdent AI.
  • Work alongside highly skilled engineers solving complex infrastructure and platform challenges at scale.
  • Join a growing organisation investing heavily in AI infrastructure, platform services, and operational innovation.

submitting your resume, you consent to the processing and storage of your personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws, for the purposes of considering your application for current and future job opportunities.

The position will help formulate strategies supporting long-term planning, new project initiation, and engagement with emerging customers. In addition, this role will perform assessment of air vehicle performance, weight, cost, and operational assessment. The position will support the development and evaluation of new aircraft concepts against user requirements, assess ongoing aircraft development programs, and provide technical expertise to TDD for future air vehicle concepts and exploratory design initiatives.

  • Represent CD&A as an aircraft design subject matter expert (SME) at meetings, industry forums, program reviews, technology demonstrations, and operational tests.

  • U.S. Citizen.

Preferred Qualifications:

Location: This is a remote, part-time, TOC position with flexible, on-demand hours that vary based on contract needs and candidate availability.

At MEDvidi, the Automation team builds and operates a mix of AI and conventional product features that automate clinical and operational workflows - from AI-drafted medical documentation to automated resolution of patient issues, intake verification flows, provider tooling, and the backend pipelines behind them. We free clinicians and operations from manual work a machine can do reliably and safely, in a domain where mistakes have real clinical and compliance consequences.

It's a full-stack product team, not an AI lab: we ship UI, backend workflows, integrations, and AI features side by side, and we measure them the same way.

The team works closely with Product, Engineering, MedOps, Clinical people. We're hiring an Product Analyst to own analytics for the team end-to-end as our automated surface area grows.

The role

You'll be the Product Analyst for the team - across everything we ship, both classical product features and AI-powered ones. You'll turn the production behavior of our systems into evidence the team can act on: which parts work, where they fail silently, and what to fix next. The work blends product analytics, AI evaluation, and operational analysis.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full product analytics stack for features the team ships - discovery and sizing, experiment design and analysis, funnel and adoption analysis, post-release impact assessment - across both AI-powered and conventional product features.
  • Analyze production behavior of AI and automation workflows across clinical and operational journeys.
  • Investigate hallucinations, silent failures, and quality degradation in AI-generated output.
  • Work directly with logs, transcripts, generated artifacts, and operational data to find patterns dashboards miss.
  • Design evaluations for AI quality - both automated and human review - and close the loop into prompt and product changes.
  • Build monitoring and dashboards for AI and automation health, and the operational metrics they roll up to.
  • Measure business and operational impact of automation initiatives and surface the risks they introduce.
  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Clinical, MedOps, and Legal to support fast decisions under ambiguity.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in Product Analytics/Operational Analytics/Data Analytics, or analytics roles within complex production systems.
  • Understanding of AI, ML, and LLM systems.
  • Hands-on experience evaluating LLM or AI output - prompt iteration, eval frameworks and human review pipelines is a strong plus.
  • Effective, structured written and verbal communication - able to turn analysis into crisp, decision-ready writeups that non-analysts can act on.
  • Comfort in ambiguous, fast-changing environments where ground truth often has to be constructed.
  • Strong product / operational analytics background, comfortable owning metrics end-to-end and writing SQL and Python code against messy production data.
  • Fluent Russian; English level B2 or higher,
  • Ability to work CET-overlapping hours in a B2B format.

Nice to Have

  • Experience evaluating LLM outputs or AI systems.

What we offer

  • High-impact work in a product-driven medical tech company
  • Startup environment: fast iteration, high ownership, minimal bureaucracy

About Thatch

For most people, health insurance is something that happens to them: a plan chosen by someone else, with little room to fit their life. Thatch is changing that. We help companies give every employee a real healthcare budget instead of a one-size-fits-all plan, so people can choose the coverage and care that works for them, and employers get predictable costs they can control.

It’s a simple idea, but making it real means solving hard problems across healthcare, payments, and technology, and we’re just getting started. We look for people who like solving complex problems, use good judgment, and are comfortable working through ambiguity. People here care deeply about our customers, take real responsibility for what gets built, and are driven by doing work that matters.

About the role

Thatch is changing how health benefits work. We're building software that makes it easier for businesses to offer health coverage and gives employees more choice and control.

We're looking for a Data Scientist to help our Product and Operations teams understand how people use Thatch and where we can make the biggest impact. You'll own the data models and metrics behind our product, from plan shopping and enrollment to reimbursements and everyday benefit usage.

You'll dig into user behavior, uncover friction, and design experiments that help us decide what to build and improve next. This is a hands-on role where you'll build the analytics foundation teams rely on, turn complex data into clear recommendations, and help shape our product strategy.

What you will do

  • Partner with Product and Operations to answer important questions and inform product priorities.
  • Define and own product metrics, from company-wide success measures to feature-level performance.
  • Analyze user journeys, engagement, and operational data to uncover friction and opportunities.
  • Design and evaluate experiments to measure the impact of product changes.
  • Build and maintain dbt models, metrics, dashboards, and analytical tools that teams rely on.
  • Improve data quality, instrumentation, and self-serve analytics so teams can make confident decisions.

What we are looking for

  • Experience using analytics, data science, and experimentation to influence product decisions.
  • Strong SQL skills and experience with dbt or similar data transformation tools.
  • Experience building analytical data models and dashboards using BI or visualization tools.
  • Proficiency in Python for analysis, experimentation, or statistical modeling.
  • Strong product judgment and the ability to turn complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
  • Comfortable working independently, navigating ambiguity, and partnering across teams.

Tools and tech stack

  • Data: Snowflake, SQL, dbt
  • Analytics: Omni, Hex, Python
  • Development: GitHub, CI/CD
  • AI: Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and other tools that help us work faster and smarter

You won't work directly in our application layer day-to-day, but familiarity with source data and event instrumentation from systems like Ruby on Rails is helpful.

Experience that stands out

  • Influencing product roadmaps and prioritization through data.
  • Building experimentation practices, including guardrail metrics, sample-size guidance, or analysis frameworks.
  • Analyzing funnels, retention, cohorts, or engagement across complex user journeys.
  • Building statistical or machine-learning models for segmentation, forecasting, propensity, or recommendations.
  • Experience in healthcare, fintech, or other regulated industries.

What to expect

We aim to move quickly, and most candidates complete the process within 2–3 weeks. You can expect:

  • An initial conversation with a recruiter.
  • A conversation with the hiring manager and a lightweight Python coding exercise.
  • A take-home analytics exercise.
  • A review of your work, a data modeling and metrics exercise with the team, and a discussion with cross-functional partners.
  • A final conversation with engineering and company leadership.
Estimated Compensation Range
$160,000—$230,000 USD
